groups.name: Consequential scope and legitimate product intent

full_original.name: Consequential scope and legitimate product intent
full_original.shared_concern: Determine the object and obligations to which a proposed decision actually applies.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Use concrete affected concerns, intended effects, artefacts and consumers rather than a discipline or category label.
full_original.activation_guard: A consequential architectural, maintenance or family-boundary decision is actually being made; a taxonomy alone activates nothing.
full_original.distinctness: Architectural significance is not maintenance-purpose classification, and neither supplies a warranted family boundary.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-001: Identify decisions whose cross-cutting consequences, dependency reach, qualities or change costs justify architectural treatment; state why each is significant rather than relying on job title or diagram level.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-002: Connect each material concern to an architectural question, a scenario or constraint and the decision that consumes it; expose conflicts and missing participation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-006: Candidate shorthand groups salient decisions, but without a scope or consequence test it does not determine what architectural work should occur.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C001: State the intended difference, affected obligations, legitimate decision maker and acceptance question before endorsing an intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C002: Use purpose labels alongside observable activity and artefact scope, permitting multiple purposes; include additive and emergency distinctions when using the 2022 terminology.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C003: Include build, configuration, data, documentation and other non-code objects only where a current or planned maintenance obligation depends on them.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C007: Candidate proposes requiring every maintenance activity to fit exactly one of four boxes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-001: State which products and foreseeable needs belong together; test shared domain assumptions against counterexamples before committing to shared production.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-002: Compare requirements, products and expert explanations; separate invariant needs, intended variation and historical accidents; record disagreement rather than infer a common core from names.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-008: Define what each feature denotes, who interprets it and how selections relate to requirements, implementation and runtime capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-042: Associate externally supplied obligations with affected assets and products, then require appropriate evidence or specialist adjudication before deriving or changing those products.

ESA:ESA-001.bearer: Consequential software structures and decisions, at a declared scope rather than a fixed diagram granularity.
ESA:ESA-001.authority: Design participants and those accountable for affected product/operating concerns. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-001.trigger: A decision can change a stakeholder outcome beyond its local implementation or would be costly to reverse.

ESA:ESA-002.bearer: Stakeholder concerns related to system-wide and boundary-level choices.
ESA:ESA-002.authority: Those making trade-offs and those who will bear their consequences; elicitors facilitate rather than acquire unilateral authority. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-002.trigger: Different users, maintainers, operators or sponsors bear materially different consequences.

ESA:ESA-006.bearer: Definitional boundary between architecture and other consequential work.
ESA:ESA-006.authority: Researchers and practitioners choosing the scope of an architectural inquiry. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-006.trigger: The label is used to claim authority over all important engineering or business matters.

ESME:ESME-C001.bearer: Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

authority.actors: Those entitled to request or rely on the behaviour, not merely the test author.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C001.trigger: A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment.

ESME:ESME-C002.bearer: Request intent and actual changed artefacts. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

authority.actors: Request owner for intention; analyst for observed activities.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C002.trigger: Classification affects estimates, authorisation, reporting or selection of maintenance evidence.

ESME:ESME-C003.bearer: Consequential code and non-code artefacts within a stated maintenance obligation.

authority.actors: Maintainer, operator and downstream consumer of the actual artefact.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-061: State where a model’s terms and rules are valid, map actual relations to other models, and make required translation or shared meaning explicit.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-068: When using the Wright/CSP formalism, establish both connector conservatism and deadlock freedom along with port/role compatibility before transferring the theorem’s deadlock-freedom result to an instantiated connector.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C026: Declare supported clients and observers, test their relevant interactions and coordinate intentional breaking transitions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C030: Name the observer, relevant environment and deliberately excluded observations before claiming behaviour preservation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C055: Declare old/new data meanings, authoritative writers and reconciliation rules; check the transfer against actual data and concurrent effects instead of equating record counts or script success with preserved meaning.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C056: State the mapping and its information-loss/invertibility conditions; preserve enough source information or choose forward repair where an inverse does not exist.

differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-012: Use the least expressive representation that preserves required distinctions; verify translations and tool support for the actual language level.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-019: State the architectural invariants required for reuse and the permitted substitutions; enforce or check them in the derivation path where the claim requires enforcement.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-046: Specify the supported language level and check semantic preservation for translations and toolchains; make unsupported constructs explicit.

groups.name: Warranted commonality and anticipatory flexibility

full_original.name: Warranted commonality and anticipatory flexibility
full_original.shared_concern: Shared production and hidden variation need credible consumers rather than speculative universality.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Examine commonality, plausible variation and its support burden against independent products or selective reuse.
full_original.activation_guard: Shared assets or future flexibility are being considered, not merely a single implementation with parameters.
full_original.distinctness: Architectural family constructibility is not a product-line economic case or a maintenance support promise.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-007: Place knowledge of a plausibly varying design decision behind an interface whose clients need not depend on that decision; separate stable obligations from hidden choices.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-013: Identify common and varying obligations across a genuine set of related systems, then arrange abstractions and uses relations to support required variants or subsets.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-049: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C029: Identify supported releases/configurations and the obligations shared or different across them; select evidence by actual support promises and interaction risk.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C052: Compare feasible interventions by preserved obligations, domain recovery, data conversion, support horizon and transition cost; do not collapse all modernisation into rewriting.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C064: Compare intervention, validation, disruption, future support and opportunity costs under plausible scenarios; retain uncertainty and identify cost bearers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C065: Defer a structural intervention when its expected value is below its cost, while retaining a trigger to revisit if demand, risk or support changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-001: State which products and foreseeable needs belong together; test shared domain assumptions against counterexamples before committing to shared production.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-002: Compare requirements, products and expert explanations; separate invariant needs, intended variation and historical accidents; record disagreement rather than infer a common core from names.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-050: Reject the universal prerequisite; use the proactive, reactive, extractive or hybrid route justified by the actual starting conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-057: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.

groups.name: Quality criteria and selected populations

full_original.name: Quality criteria and selected populations
full_original.shared_concern: An acceptable result is relative to real concerns, observers, configurations and hard constraints.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Use explicit response conditions and representative product/maintenance scenarios; keep sacrifices and excluded populations visible.
full_original.activation_guard: A quality or benefit claim supports a consequential choice; small concrete examples may discharge the concern.
full_original.distinctness: Architectural response measures, maintenance-task outcomes and family coverage cannot be added into a universal quality score.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-014: Express a quality concern through stimulus, source, environment, affected artefact, response and response measure, tailoring detail to the decision being made.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-015: Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-016: Connect a tactic to the model parameters it changes and to the response sought; account for interactions, overhead and assumptions that make the causal explanation plausible.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-017: Separate hard constraints from preferences, compare effects on multiple concerns and make the chosen sacrifice explicit; do not aggregate away unacceptable consequences.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-019: Independent maximisation ignores interaction and feasibility; it is not retained as an engineering rule.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-028: Bring business/mission drivers, architecture and quality scenarios into a structured review to identify assumptions, risks, sensitivity points and trade-offs that need a decision.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-030: Choose a focused prototype, simulation or analytic model for the uncertainty at hand; calibrate it where possible and distinguish omitted behaviour from demonstrated behaviour.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-062: Allow a concrete user-interaction concern to change architecture when satisfying it requires system state, control, responsiveness or recoverability beyond visual layout.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C030: Name the observer, relevant environment and deliberately excluded observations before claiming behaviour preservation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C034: Name the recurring maintenance task and expected improvement, compare transition and opportunity costs, intervene within a justified bound and review observed task outcomes before continuing or expanding.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C035: Use metrics to identify questions and compare a declared local objective; cross-check against actual task cost and requirements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C038: Separately establish evidence for the intended new effect and the consequential behaviours that must survive, with uncertainty stated for both.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C039: Trace acceptance expectations to independent requirements, adjudicated behaviour, domain properties or credible reference evidence; state gaps and conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-010: Validate constraints against representative positive and negative product scenarios, expert knowledge and implementation evidence; explicitly record unmodelled conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-024: Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-025: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.

ESA:ESA-014.bearer: Quality requirements at the system or affected architectural element.
ESA:ESA-014.authority: Stakeholders, designers, evaluators and testers consuming a shared condition. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-014.trigger: A quality term such as fast, secure, usable or modifiable must discriminate between designs.

ESA:ESA-015.bearer: Scenario population, sampling and prioritisation at evaluation scope.
ESA:ESA-015.authority: Evaluators and affected participants, including dissenting or absent-user representatives where warranted. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-015.trigger: An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

ESA:ESA-016.bearer: Architectural tactic acting on performance, availability, security, modifiability or other modelled qualities.
ESA:ESA-016.authority: Designers selecting interventions and evaluators testing their consequences. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-016.trigger: A structural or behavioural intervention is proposed to improve a quality attribute.

ESA:ESA-017.bearer: Multi-quality architectural alternatives and external constraints.
ESA:ESA-017.authority: Affected stakeholders and authorised trade-off decision makers. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-017.trigger: Improving one response can worsen another or transfer cost to a different stakeholder.

ESA:ESA-018.bearer: Empirical evidence about realised architectural behaviour, not just models.
ESA:ESA-018.authority: Testers, operators and decision makers relying on measured outcomes. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-018.trigger: A prototype, benchmark, trace or field observation is being used to accept an architecture.

ESA:ESA-019.bearer: An inadmissible general optimisation claim over architectural qualities.
ESA:ESA-019.authority: Anyone interpreting a multi-quality improvement claim. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-019.trigger: A proposal claims every quality improves without defining resource, stakeholder or environmental boundaries.

ESA:ESA-028.bearer: Multi-quality evaluation of an architectural candidate.
ESA:ESA-028.authority: Stakeholders, evaluation facilitators and people authorised to accept or mitigate the identified risks. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-028.trigger: Several consequential qualities interact and missing assumptions justify a facilitated multi-stakeholder review.

ESA:ESA-030.bearer: Prototype, simulation or analytic model tied to a real architectural decision.
ESA:ESA-030.authority: Designers and evaluators responsible for uncertainty reduction, not for treating an experiment as automatic release authority. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-030.trigger: A consequential prediction cannot be judged adequately by reasoning or existing observations alone.

ESA:ESA-062.bearer: Coupling between user interaction and architectural state/control mechanisms.
ESA:ESA-062.authority: Users or their representatives, interaction designers and system engineers. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-062.trigger: A user scenario cannot be met by presentation changes alone.

ESME:ESME-C030.bearer: Pre/post implementation and relevant external context. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.actors: Specified outputs, exceptions, timing, resources, reflection, layout or persistence as warranted.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C030.trigger: A transformation is justified as non-functional or structure-only.

ESME:ESME-C034.bearer: Structure, expected change scenarios and intervention effort. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.actors: Future maintainers and those bearing current conversion cost.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C034.trigger: Repeated or credible upcoming work is materially hindered by the current structure and a feasible change may improve it.

ESME:ESME-C035.bearer: Metric definition, affected structure and real maintenance tasks. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.actors: Maintainer or planner interpreting the signal.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C035.trigger: A metric might reveal a bottleneck not already understood.

ESME:ESME-C038.bearer: New objective, preservation set, tests and other evidence. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.

authority.actors: Requesting stakeholder and existing consumers.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C038.trigger: Any intervention changes or risks a relied-on behaviour.

ESME:ESME-C039.bearer: The provenance and scope of the observation or acceptance criterion.
ESME:ESME-C039.authority: Domain experts and obligation owners adjudicate expectations; tests and agents produce evidence, not authority.
ESME:ESME-C039.trigger: Test results support a change decision or a test expectation itself changes.

ESPLE:ESPLE-010.bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
ESPLE:ESPLE-010.authority: Domain experts and product stakeholders validate meaning; technical extraction contributes evidence but cannot supply every missing obligation. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-010.trigger: A variability model is relied upon to accept or exclude product choices.

ESPLE:ESPLE-023.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-023.authority: Assurance reviewers and release decision-makers consume bounded claims; analysts do not acquire release authority by producing evidence. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-023.trigger: A model, test, proof or analysis result is used to justify a product or family decision.

ESPLE:ESPLE-024.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-024.authority: Feature developers and assurance engineers exchange interaction hypotheses and failures; product owners decide acceptable residual risk. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-024.trigger: Features share state, resources, protocols, build choices or behavioural assumptions.

ESPLE:ESPLE-025.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.authority: Test planners and assurance consumers choose the coverage trade-off; a sampler cannot declare all unsampled products correct. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.trigger: Full enumeration is infeasible and a bounded sample can provide useful assurance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-028.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-028.authority: Product acceptance and operational stakeholders decide readiness; core-asset maintainers supply evidence but do not replace local obligations. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-028.trigger: A product is delivered, deployed or materially changed.

ESPLE:ESPLE-036.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.authority: Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.trigger: An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

groups.name: Model, tool and actual-product assurance layers

full_original.name: Model, tool and actual-product assurance layers
full_original.shared_concern: A valid representation or successful analysis is not automatically a valid realised system.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Keep model adequacy, encoding/engine validity, correspondence and actual-subject evidence separate.
full_original.activation_guard: A view, solver, generator or transformation is being used as evidence beyond its own object.
full_original.distinctness: Description conformance, SAT, engine tests and product acceptance establish different claims.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-003: Keep intended structure, its representation and claims about the actual system distinguishable; attach a basis and observation scope to assertions of correspondence.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-020: Select viewpoints by the concerns and decisions they enable, then create only the views needed to communicate or analyse those concerns.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-021: Identify how entities and relations in different views correspond, then check consequential consistency and the link to implementation/configuration/operation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-022: Use a formal description when a consequential property can be expressed and analysed under a tractable model; keep the guarantee, assumptions and implementation mapping explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-024: Combine appropriate static, configuration, dynamic and human evidence to reconstruct only the architectural facts needed; label extraction scope, ambiguity and unobserved behaviour.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-031: A review can establish that a process occurred and risks were considered; it cannot by itself guarantee the real system under unexamined conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-038: Check a declared, justified architectural constraint against appropriately extracted or observed relationships; attach the relevant baseline, mapping and evidence to each finding.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-059: Conformance of an architecture description is not admitted as a certificate that the actual architecture satisfies stakeholder concerns.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C016: Recover the rationale and abstractions needed for the change by checking code/behaviour against knowledgeable people and domain evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C017: Produce or refresh a description only when a maintainer or downstream consumer needs it, and check it against the current subject.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C018: Distinguish analysis that changes a representation or understanding from an intervention that alters the subject system; describe the actual abstraction level and effects.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C021: Choose static, dynamic, historical and human views for the question; reconcile consequential disagreement instead of treating agreement or diagram completeness as proof.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C032: Exercise relevant tool/version transformations with targeted counterexamples, compilation, differential or other justified checks; investigate disagreements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C033: Check the actual transformed baseline using relevant semantic reasoning, tests or comparison; invalidate earlier evidence when consequential inputs change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C039: Trace acceptance expectations to independent requirements, adjudicated behaviour, domain properties or credible reference evidence; state gaps and conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C045: Candidate promotes test passage to complete correctness without proving coverage and oracle adequacy.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-009: Check the model's declared semantics for consistency and investigate diagnoses relative to intended configurations; report the exact model and solver interpretation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-010: Validate constraints against representative positive and negative product scenarios, expert knowledge and implementation evidence; explicitly record unmodelled conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-017: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-046: Specify the supported language level and check semantic preservation for translations and toolchains; make unsupported constructs explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-051: Reject artefact sufficiency; require meaningful features, usable constraints, a relation to realisation and an actual configuration or change consumer.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-052: Reject the implication. Keep model consistency, realisation correctness and product behaviour as separate claims with explicit connecting premises.

ESA:ESA-003.bearer: Intended architecture, architecture description and realised software/configuration as separate referents.
ESA:ESA-003.authority: Implementers, reviewers and operators relying on architectural claims. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-003.trigger: A decision depends on a diagram, repository model, recovered graph or architect’s account being true of the real system.

ESA:ESA-020.bearer: Architecture descriptions and viewpoint conventions at concern-specific abstraction levels.
ESA:ESA-020.authority: Description authors and the actual stakeholders or analysts using each view. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-020.trigger: One representation obscures materially different structural, runtime, deployment or development questions.

ESA:ESA-021.bearer: Cross-view and description–implementation relations, not visual layout similarity.
ESA:ESA-021.authority: Design, deployment, development and evaluation participants relying on combined descriptions. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-021.trigger: A decision combines claims from several views or uses a model as evidence about implementation.

ESA:ESA-022.authority: Modellers, verification specialists and engineers responsible for implementing the model’s assumptions. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-022.trigger: An interaction/configuration property justifies stronger analysis than informal review or testing alone.

ESA:ESA-024.bearer: Inferred architectural structures and behaviours from realised artefacts.
ESA:ESA-024.authority: Maintainers, migration designers and reviewers who need specific missing knowledge. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-024.trigger: Reliable architectural knowledge is missing or an existing description is suspect.

ESA:ESA-031.bearer: Inference from evaluation process completion to realised performance or correctness.
ESA:ESA-031.authority: People accepting a design or relying on its review status. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-031.trigger: An approval, risk list or completed workshop is used as conclusive evidence that the system will meet its qualities.

ESA:ESA-038.bearer: Intended constraints mapped to realised static or dynamic architectural relationships.
ESA:ESA-038.authority: Constraint owners, implementers and reviewers able to accept or revise the affected design. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-038.trigger: A system depends on a structural or behavioural restriction that implementation changes might violate.

ESA:ESA-059.bearer: Boundary between architecture-description requirements and realised architecture quality.
ESA:ESA-059.authority: Standards users, reviewers and recipients of assurance claims. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-059.trigger: A standards claim about documentation is offered as proof of performance, security, maintainability or other operating quality.

ESME:ESME-C016.bearer: Implementation, domain rules, historical decisions and tacit operational knowledge. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: Domain expert and successor maintainer, not solely the analysis tool.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C016.trigger: Undocumented behaviour or lost intent makes structural reconstruction insufficient.

ESME:ESME-C017.bearer: Documentation and its source artefact/version. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: The intended reader performing a named maintenance or operational task.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C017.trigger: A useful explanation is missing, stale or inaccessible to an actual consumer.

ESME:ESME-C018.bearer: Use source, generated artefacts, build/configuration state, execution traces, relevant history and rationale where each is needed to answer Q.
ESME:ESME-C018.authority: Analysts recover evidence; authorised maintainers perform transformations; consumers must not infer one from the other.
ESME:ESME-C018.trigger: A recovery or modernisation activity is proposed, evaluated or handed off.

ESME:ESME-C021.bearer: Extracted components/relations, execution observations and build mapping. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: Analyst and maintainer using the recovered view.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C021.trigger: A single view leaves a consequential question unresolved or independent views disagree.

ESME:ESME-C032.bearer: The selected transformation engine, implementation and version.

authority.actors: Tool user and reviewer who rely on the engine’s preservation claim.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C032.trigger: A transformation engine is new, changed, historically faulty or used outside its validated envelope.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-020: Select viewpoints by the concerns and decisions they enable, then create only the views needed to communicate or analyse those concerns.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-023: Completing a prescribed view set regardless of its consumers is ceremony, not a generally useful mechanism.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-032: Preserve the context, selected option, significant alternatives, consequences and assumptions that a future actor needs to understand or revise a consequential decision.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-033: Keep a decision’s status and reopening conditions visible; distinguish superseding it from erasing the evidence that once justified it.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-037: Document quantity alone is not retained as a proxy for architectural knowledge, correctness or maintenance value.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-041: Recovered structure cannot by itself establish the stakeholders, alternatives or rationale behind it; inferred intent must be labelled and corroborated.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-064: Provide a coherent explanation of why the current design is defensible while separately labelling historical records and reconstructed reasoning; do not make a tidy story into fabricated provenance.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C016: Recover the rationale and abstractions needed for the change by checking code/behaviour against knowledgeable people and domain evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C017: Produce or refresh a description only when a maintainer or downstream consumer needs it, and check it against the current subject.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C019: Candidate blocks every local change until the entire system and all tacit intent are recovered.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C021: Choose static, dynamic, historical and human views for the question; reconcile consequential disagreement instead of treating agreement or diagram completeness as proof.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C070: Retain the decision-relevant reasons, alternatives and accepted limitations in a form successors can locate and test against current conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-002: Compare requirements, products and expert explanations; separate invariant needs, intended variation and historical accidents; record disagreement rather than infer a common core from names.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-005: Return a product observation with its configuration, asset baseline and consequence; decide whether to repair the core, adjust a constraint, retain an exception or revise scope.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-014: Preserve the feature-to-artefact relations needed for derivation, change impact and diagnosis, including build selection, generator input and shared implementation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-018: Treat non-code work products as reusable assets where products actually consume them, with compatible versioning and variation information.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-034: Recover candidate features and constraints from multiple artefact types, preserve existing valid domain knowledge and review recovered relations against product intent.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-051: Reject artefact sufficiency; require meaningful features, usable constraints, a relation to realisation and an actual configuration or change consumer.

ESPLE:ESPLE-034.authority: Reverse engineers and domain experts jointly assess extracted candidates; extraction alone cannot decide that historical differences are valuable. ESPLE:ESPLE-034.trigger: Consolidating variants, repairing stale models or reducing dependence on tacit configuration knowledge.

full_original.name: Authority is not evidence or tooling
full_original.shared_concern: Knowing, proposing, accepting evidence and executing an effect do not automatically convey one another's decision rights.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Retain existing scoped decision rights and negotiated obligations at the consequential handoff.
full_original.activation_guard: A decision affects another actor, product, baseline or external state; one authorised actor can discharge several functions.
full_original.distinctness: Architecture trade-off authority, maintenance action authority and shared-asset arbitration remain context-supplied, not merged into a new owner.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-005: Make it clear who can accept a consequential trade-off, who must be consulted and who can execute it; neither identifying a concern nor holding a meeting grants permission to act.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-035: Allow local choices inside explicit shared contracts and escalate or negotiate only decisions that change cross-boundary consequences; preserve a way to resolve conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-039: For a deviation, decide whether the implementation is harmful, the model is stale, the change is authorised improvement or evidence is insufficient; revise the correct object.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-042: Zero departures from any historical model is not admitted as a general quality requirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-048: An improved local objective neither authorises an architectural change nor establishes its external consequences.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-063: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C001: State the intended difference, affected obligations, legitimate decision maker and acceptance question before endorsing an intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C038: Separately establish evidence for the intended new effect and the consequential behaviours that must survive, with uncertainty stated for both.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C071: Make responsibility and decision rights clear enough to resolve overlapping changes and support requests without assuming exclusive code ownership.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C094: Distinguish proposing a change, accepting its evidence and executing consequential actions; bind each to actual legitimate capability and any limited delegation. Authorisation of a goal does not automatically transfer deployment or external-state powers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C096: Candidate claims that successful generated patches eliminate the need to establish intent, residual evidence or accountable action.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C097: Candidate elevates all observed legacy behaviour to a perpetual requirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C098: Revise a method, threshold or oracle only for an authorised failure/benefit hypothesis or separately authorised objective change, using evidence not constituted merely by the candidate satisfying its newly chosen rule; preserve unrelated predecessor obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C101: Strip the mandatory ritual while preserving appropriate authorisation, consultation and evidence; use a fuller forum only when conflicts or obligations require it.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-004: Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-006: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-039: Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-041: Identify who controls assets, proposals, interfaces and releases; distinguish contractual or negotiated compatibility from internal derivation authority; export bounded interfaces rather than fictitious central control.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-042: Associate externally supplied obligations with affected assets and products, then require appropriate evidence or specialist adjudication before deriving or changing those products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-047: Treat generated changes as proposals; validate syntax, constraints, semantic intent, realisation and product obligations using appropriate independent checks before acceptance.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-060: Reject self-authorising control; separately establish observation, actual actuation capability, external permission and the expected consequence.

ESA:ESA-005.bearer: Consequential decisions and commitments at organisational/software interfaces.
ESA:ESA-005.authority: Trade-off decision makers, implementers and affected consumers; authority is supplied by the real context, not this ledger. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-005.trigger: A change alters commitments or transfers risk/cost across roles, teams or external parties.

ESA:ESA-035.bearer: Architectural decision allocation across component, product and team boundaries.
ESA:ESA-035.authority: Local teams and those accountable for shared constraints; delegation is contextual rather than asserted by the method. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-035.trigger: Multiple teams need autonomy but share users, data, quality limits or release obligations.

ESA:ESA-039.bearer: Deviations between intended, documented and realised architectures over time.
ESA:ESA-039.authority: Maintainers, evaluators and authorised architecture decision makers. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-039.trigger: A realised relationship departs from an architectural baseline.

ESA:ESA-042.bearer: Historical model compliance as an unconditional architectural objective.
ESA:ESA-042.authority: Reviewers and maintainers choosing whether the implementation or baseline should change. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-042.trigger: A historical rule is enforced despite changed requirements or evidence that its violation is an improvement.

ESA:ESA-048.bearer: Self-authorisation claim for metric-driven architectural change.
ESA:ESA-048.authority: Engineers and operators interpreting automated recommendations or actions. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-048.trigger: A controller or decision-support tool treats its own score as sufficient permission and proof of success.

ESA:ESA-063.bearer: Adaptation controller, monitoring model, policy and their revision boundaries.
ESA:ESA-063.authority: Engineers/operators authorised to revise control rules; self-revision is only within an independently justified delegation. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-063.trigger: A running adaptation mechanism or its evidence/decision rules are being revised.

ESME:ESME-C001.bearer: Change request, affected behaviour and requirements history. Requests, contracts, code, data, configuration, manuals and maintenance readiness can all be affected.

authority.actors: Those entitled to request or rely on the behaviour, not merely the test author.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C001.trigger: A request, discovered defect or environmental pressure proposes changing an existing commitment.

ESME:ESME-C038.bearer: New objective, preservation set, tests and other evidence. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.

authority.actors: Requesting stakeholder and existing consumers.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C038.trigger: Any intervention changes or risks a relied-on behaviour.

ESME:ESME-C071.bearer: Change requests, affected components and decision responsibilities. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Contributors, maintainers and downstream users seeking a decision.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C071.trigger: Multiple contributors or support paths create ambiguity about acceptance, review or incident response.

ESME:ESME-C094.bearer: The acceptance decision and execution powers for a concrete intervention.
ESME:ESME-C094.authority: The legitimate request/obligation owner, acceptance decision maker and action executor may differ. A goal approval or generated insight does not delegate deployment or external-state powers. One capable actor may hold all roles within the agreed scope.
ESME:ESME-C094.trigger: An actor or automated tool proposes, accepts or executes a change, especially when these functions cross authority boundaries.

ESME:ESME-C096.bearer: Automated workflow, generated changes and live obligations. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.

authority.actors: Maintainers and affected users, including those bearing external effects.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C096.trigger: A benchmark or demonstration is used to justify unrestricted self-directed production maintenance.

ESME:ESME-C097.bearer: Legacy behaviour, actual reliance and current requirements. Bind tests, results, build inputs, artefact identity, environment, deployed versions and relevant data state.

authority.actors: Affected legitimate users, not only historical code output.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C097.trigger: A characterisation test or compatibility argument blocks correction of an obsolete, accidental or harmful behaviour.

ESME:ESME-C098.bearer: A proposed revision of a maintenance method or oracle relative to the preceding obligation.
ESME:ESME-C098.authority: Method owners and affected consumers approve changes; the method or agent cannot authorise its own broader powers.
ESME:ESME-C098.trigger: The method is failing or disproportionately costly, technology changes, or a candidate proposes to revise the expectation by which it will be judged.

ESME:ESME-C101.bearer: Identify the system/configuration being changed and any non-code artefact needed to interpret the request. A source commit alone may omit deployed data and obligations.
ESME:ESME-C101.authority: Existing legitimate decision authority remains; removal of ceremony does not permit unauthorised changes.
ESME:ESME-C101.trigger: Adjudicate when the presence of a board is treated as the maintenance property itself.

ESPLE:ESPLE-004.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-004.authority: Asset developers and product developers need reciprocal access to decisions; management supplies resources rather than treating a model as authority. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-004.trigger: At least one asset or production decision is intended to serve several products.

ESPLE:ESPLE-006.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-006.authority: Product and core maintainers agree who carries future changes; permission to diverge is not permission to misrepresent family assurance. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-006.trigger: A product obligation cannot be met adequately through the current shared assets without disproportionate disruption.

ESPLE:ESPLE-039.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-039.authority: Product and core decision-makers exchange impact and priority information; evidence of a technical opportunity is separate from authority to act. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-039.trigger: Shared changes affect products with different priorities or authorities.

ESPLE:ESPLE-041.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.authority: Platform maintainers and external participants negotiate evidence and compatibility; one organisation cannot unilaterally authorise changes to autonomous derivatives. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.trigger: Suppliers, open-source participants or independent platform users determine material variation.

ESPLE:ESPLE-042.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-042.authority: Product owners, relevant specialists and asset maintainers exchange obligations and impact evidence; SPLE analysis does not grant legal permission or certify security. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-042.trigger: Supplier conditions, security requirements, licences, regulation or support commitments constrain valid product use.

ESPLE:ESPLE-047.bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-047.authority: Modellers, maintainers and product acceptance decision-makers review the candidate; model fluency confers no mutation or release permission. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-047.trigger: Learned tools assist feature modelling, configuration advice, migration or variant generation.

ESPLE:ESPLE-060.bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-060.authority: Operators and accountable product authorities decide deployment; the proof author cannot create authority through notation. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-060.trigger: A formal or generated controller is proposed for real runtime configuration.

groups.name: Practical capacity and coordination

full_original.name: Practical capacity and coordination
full_original.shared_concern: Responsibility must remain actionable with willing capacity and adequate cross-boundary communication.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Match accepted shared work and dependent decisions to actual capability; resolve conflicts without prescribing team topology.
full_original.activation_guard: Cross-team dependencies, turnover or shared-product demand threaten delivery or support.
full_original.distinctness: Conceptual integrity is not centralised staffing; a knowledge metric and an organisation chart do not prove capacity.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-004: Keep the user-visible and developer-facing concepts and essential invariants coherent across decisions, while allowing local variation that does not damage them.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-012: Place boundaries by considering change coupling, communication, translation and operation costs together; compare local and distributed alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-034: Identify consequential technical/work dependencies and arrange adequate communication across the people who must coordinate them; test the actual coordination problem rather than copying an organisation chart.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-035: Allow local choices inside explicit shared contracts and escalate or negotiate only decisions that change cross-boundary consequences; preserve a way to resolve conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-036: No deterministic rule mapping an organisation chart to software architecture is admitted; communication and technical structures influence each other under contingent conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C004: At a transfer or continuity risk, establish that an actual willing recipient has the knowledge, access, time and practical ability to perform representative supported work; use explanation, supervised work or equivalent evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C011: Use observed comprehension, review and recovery demand to constrain change intake and invest in knowledge when understanding becomes a bottleneck.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C012: Candidate fixes staffing, effort or delivery-rate predictions as invariant across organisations and tool/environment changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C066: Identify who gains now and who must later maintain, migrate or absorb risk; involve affected decision makers to the extent needed for legitimate trade-offs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C071: Make responsibility and decision rights clear enough to resolve overlapping changes and support requests without assuming exclusive code ownership.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C072: Align promised support, intake and update obligations with available willing capacity; negotiate reduced scope, sponsorship, transfer or retirement when infeasible.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C073: Use the estimate to ask who can actually support critical work; verify with maintainers rather than treating a computed number as a failure probability.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-004: Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-039: Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-040: Align skills, capacity, incentives and cost allocation with the intended shared-production responsibilities; scale commitments to actual capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-041: Identify who controls assets, proposals, interfaces and releases; distinguish contractual or negotiated compatibility from internal derivation authority; export bounded interfaces rather than fictitious central control.

groups.name: Lifecycle alternatives, cost bearers and uncertainty

full_original.name: Lifecycle alternatives, cost bearers and uncertainty
full_original.shared_concern: A locally attractive decision can shift unacceptable cost or violate a population-specific obligation.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Compare feasible alternatives over the relevant horizon, respect hard constraints, and expose uncertainty and who bears costs.
full_original.activation_guard: Investment, continuation or retirement depends on expected value; qualitative comparison is legitimate.
full_original.distinctness: Architecture quality, maintenance effort, variability economics and sustainability boundaries are separate inputs, not additive independent benefits.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-017: Separate hard constraints from preferences, compare effects on multiple concerns and make the chosen sacrifice explicit; do not aggregate away unacceptable consequences.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-026: Compare feasible architectural options, including retaining the present design or a smaller intervention, against the same concerns and assumptions; expose excluded options.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-029: Establish feasible options and hard constraints first, then explore plausible costs, utilities, dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating one estimated ratio as an objective answer.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-043: Identify the specific structural compromise, its current benefit, the future work or recurring penalty it may cause and the plausible cost of remedy; distinguish observed interest from a prediction.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-049: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-055: Declare the sustainability concern and system/lifecycle boundary, then evaluate architectural alternatives against measurable impacts and competing constraints rather than assuming a fashionable deployment is greener.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-056: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C034: Name the recurring maintenance task and expected improvement, compare transition and opportunity costs, intervene within a justified bound and review observed task outcomes before continuing or expanding.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C051: Assess obligations, supportability and change cost directly; treat age as a possible clue, not proof that replacement is needed.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C052: Compare feasible interventions by preserved obligations, domain recovery, data conversion, support horizon and transition cost; do not collapse all modernisation into rewriting.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C062: Identify a concrete design/implementation condition and the future work that makes its liability actual; distinguish defects, missing features and ordinary maintenance.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C064: Compare intervention, validation, disruption, future support and opportunity costs under plausible scenarios; retain uncertainty and identify cost bearers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C065: Defer a structural intervention when its expected value is below its cost, while retaining a trigger to revisit if demand, risk or support changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C066: Identify who gains now and who must later maintain, migrate or absorb risk; involve affected decision makers to the extent needed for legitimate trade-offs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C067: Candidate requires all debt items to be eliminated irrespective of future use, opportunity cost or retirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C068: Candidate treats a universal index or tool-generated principal as proof of maintenance return.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C069: Reject the guarantee; require a task-specific causal account and proportionate outcome evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C081: Choose continued unchanged operation where current obligations, support conditions and expected value do not justify intervention; keep only relevant observation triggers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C105: Evaluate the combined inquiry, validation, coordination and support arrangement against live obligations and observed outcomes; consolidate, substitute or retire controls whose consumer or protection has ended or whose cost is dominated, without silently waiving the outcome.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-049: No general mechanism supports the universal threshold. Replace the claim with a horizon-specific comparison of investment, derivation, coordination and support costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-057: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-059: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-061: Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.

full_original.name: Preservation and deliberate revision
full_original.shared_concern: Preserve legitimate observer obligations while permitting authorised changes; historical equality is not the objective.

full_original.distinctness: A stable name, unchanged feature-set language or historic architecture does not establish behavioural compatibility.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-008: Express consequential assumptions about state, control, ordering, data meaning, faults and side effects at the interface; check the assumptions actually relied on by both sides.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-038: Check a declared, justified architectural constraint against appropriately extracted or observed relationships; attach the relevant baseline, mapping and evidence to each finding.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-039: For a deviation, decide whether the implementation is harmful, the model is stale, the change is authorised improvement or evidence is insufficient; revise the correct object.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-042: Zero departures from any historical model is not admitted as a general quality requirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C001: State the intended difference, affected obligations, legitimate decision maker and acceptance question before endorsing an intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C026: Declare supported clients and observers, test their relevant interactions and coordinate intentional breaking transitions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C027: Candidate accepts or rejects a dependency solely from its version number as proof of actual compatibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C030: Name the observer, relevant environment and deliberately excluded observations before claiming behaviour preservation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C037: Record relevant existing observations to expose relied-on behaviour and candidate regressions, then determine which expectations are legitimately retained or deliberately changed.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C038: Separately establish evidence for the intended new effect and the consequential behaviours that must survive, with uncertainty stated for both.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C097: Candidate elevates all observed legacy behaviour to a perpetual requirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-006: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-030: Compare old and new model semantics using an explicit feature correspondence; classify preserved, added and removed configurations before selecting migration or regression work.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-031: Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-058: Reject the equivalence; preserve or explicitly change feature intent and verify the actual migrated product's obligations.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-009: Model or inspect the actual interaction mechanism—call, event, stream, shared store or protocol—and its control/data consequences instead of treating an arrow as self-explanatory.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-044: Plan migration steps that preserve required behaviour and compatibility while old and new structures coexist; include routing/data transitions and an explicit end to temporary arrangements.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-051: Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C049: Identify persistent and external effects, demonstrate the restoration, containment or forward-repair route actually promised, and reconsider remaining options before a transition invalidates them; obtain legitimate acceptance for residual irreversibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C052: Compare feasible interventions by preserved obligations, domain recovery, data conversion, support horizon and transition cost; do not collapse all modernisation into rewriting.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C053: Identify a separable responsibility and route or transfer it under a tested coexistence protocol, with a funded exit for temporary integration.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C054: Choose a single transition only when rehearsal, downtime/loss acceptance and state conversion evidence make it preferable to unsupported coexistence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C055: Declare old/new data meanings, authoritative writers and reconciliation rules; check the transfer against actual data and concurrent effects instead of equating record counts or script success with preserved meaning.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C056: State the mapping and its information-loss/invertibility conditions; preserve enough source information or choose forward repair where an inverse does not exist.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C057: Enumerate the supported intermediate combinations and constrain activation order or feature use until each combination’s obligations hold.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C058: Keep temporary gateways and duplicate operation only while they protect a live obligation; before declaring completion or removing them, check residual consumers, data authority, supported versions and recovery needs, then close the old path or explicitly reclassify enduring coexistence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C059: Candidate forbids replacement regardless of support constraints, separability or transition evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C061: Candidate treats a code revert as proof that all deployed consequences are undone.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C104: At the join of concurrent edits, mixed versions, data mappings and responsibility transfers, identify reachable combinations that matter to supported obligations and validate, isolate or prohibit those combinations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-006: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-016: Define applicable deltas, their dependencies or order and the validity conditions of each modification; verify the resulting product rather than assuming arbitrary edits commute.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-031: Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-033: State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-044: Check the transition path, quiescence or state transfer and actual controllability; preserve safety requirements throughout the operating phase or enter a separately justified safe reconfiguration phase.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-061: Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.
