groups.name: Observation, feedback and revision

full_original.name: Observation, feedback and revision
full_original.shared_concern: Changed observations can reopen assumptions rather than merely report a score.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Return a scoped observation to an actor able to change the relevant decision, evidence claim, constraint or support choice.
full_original.activation_guard: A material observation or assumption change can alter justified action; no fixed feedback cadence follows.
full_original.distinctness: Product-to-core feedback, architectural fitness checks, regression feedback and distribution drift have different signals and consumers.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-033: Keep a decision’s status and reopening conditions visible; distinguish superseding it from erasing the evidence that once justified it.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-039: For a deviation, decide whether the implementation is harmful, the model is stale, the change is authorised improvement or evidence is insufficient; revise the correct object.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-045: Use maintained checks to detect changes in selected architectural characteristics, and periodically challenge whether the checks still measure the concern and preserve competing constraints.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-046: Observe the running system, interpret observations in an architecture model, choose among allowed changes and execute them through available effectors; keep system-specific translation explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-063: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C008: Observe changes in use, expectations and constraints; decide whether adaptation, servicing, unchanged operation or retirement best preserves justified usefulness.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C022: State the consequential artefacts, consumers, dependencies and assumptions potentially affected; challenge the boundary in proportion to missed-effect consequence and reopen it when counterevidence appears.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C047: Integrate at a cadence suited to actual dependencies and run evidence that can detect meaningful interaction failures; communicate failures to someone able to act.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C048: Choose an isolatable population, meaningful observation window and attributable metrics; stop or revise on adverse or insufficient evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C092: Monitor the relevant data/environment and outcome assumptions; reconsider preservation and regression evidence when those assumptions shift.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C098: Revise a method, threshold or oracle only for an authorised failure/benefit hypothesis or separately authorised objective change, using evidence not constituted merely by the candidate satisfying its newly chosen rule; preserve unrelated predecessor obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C103: Track the consequential assumptions under which evidence supports a downstream claim; when an assumption changes, narrow or invalidate only dependent claims and obtain adequate replacement evidence before consequential reuse.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-005: Return a product observation with its configuration, asset baseline and consequence; decide whether to repair the core, adjust a constraint, retain an exception or revise scope.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-030: Compare old and new model semantics using an explicit feature correspondence; classify preserved, added and removed configurations before selecting migration or regression work.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-032: Identify affected products and assumptions, select appropriate regression evidence and coordinate propagation, exceptions or supported parallel versions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-035: Reassess test-configuration validity and purpose after model change; choose repair, fresh generation or targeted new-product tests according to regression and novelty objectives.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-043: Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.

ESA:ESA-018.authority: Testers, operators and decision makers relying on measured outcomes. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-018.trigger: A prototype, benchmark, trace or field observation is being used to accept an architecture.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-015: Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-021: Identify how entities and relations in different views correspond, then check consequential consistency and the link to implementation/configuration/operation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-022: Use a formal description when a consequential property can be expressed and analysed under a tractable model; keep the guarantee, assumptions and implementation mapping explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-030: Choose a focused prototype, simulation or analytic model for the uncertainty at hand; calibrate it where possible and distinguish omitted behaviour from demonstrated behaviour.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-033: Keep a decision’s status and reopening conditions visible; distinguish superseding it from erasing the evidence that once justified it.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-045: Use maintained checks to detect changes in selected architectural characteristics, and periodically challenge whether the checks still measure the concern and preserve competing constraints.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-054: Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-063: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C005: Identify and retain the exact baseline and configuration needed to interpret, build, compare or restore the changed system.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C025: Represent the dependency types that can propagate the actual change, including build, generated, runtime, data and organisational/interface edges where consequential; distinguish observed or inferred edges from necessary ones.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C032: Exercise relevant tool/version transformations with targeted counterexamples, compilation, differential or other justified checks; investigate disagreements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C033: Check the actual transformed baseline using relevant semantic reasoning, tests or comparison; invalidate earlier evidence when consequential inputs change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C039: Trace acceptance expectations to independent requirements, adjudicated behaviour, domain properties or credible reference evidence; state gaps and conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C040: Choose a selection method only within its dependency/language envelope; escalate to broader execution when relevant changes fall outside it.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C046: Record the relevant build inputs and verify a repeatable path to the released artefact; distinguish bitwise reproducibility from functional repeatability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C084: Check that tests actually execute against the intended version, inputs and result criteria; challenge known failure/success controls and broken dependency assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C085: Record task provenance, temporal/version scope, possible training exposure and test-oracle limits; avoid treating repeated benchmark scores as independent evidence of unseen maintenance ability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C088: Bind automation evidence to the model/tool, configuration, prompts, hardware and task envelope; recheck changed assumptions before reusing the claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C091: Include data provenance, feature transformations, model versions and consequential configuration in maintenance impact and baseline reasoning.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C092: Monitor the relevant data/environment and outcome assumptions; reconsider preservation and regression evidence when those assumptions shift.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C093: Choose validation that checks the meaning and consumer of the changed artefact, including its generated or runtime effects.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C102: Bind the relevant intent, baseline, candidate, impact boundary, observation/oracle and acceptance/action authority across mechanism handoffs so that evidence is consumed for the same authorised intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C103: Track the consequential assumptions under which evidence supports a downstream claim; when an assumption changes, narrow or invalidate only dependent claims and obtain adequate replacement evidence before consequential reuse.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-017: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-021: Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-025: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-026: Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-029: Include the configuration layers relevant to the claimed result and track approximation or unsupported constructs in the extraction chain.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-035: Reassess test-configuration validity and purpose after model change; choose repair, fresh generation or targeted new-product tests according to regression and novelty objectives.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-047: Treat generated changes as proposals; validate syntax, constraints, semantic intent, realisation and product obligations using appropriate independent checks before acceptance.

groups.name: Structural intervention versus actual benefit

full_original.name: Structural intervention versus actual benefit
full_original.shared_concern: A structural label, metric improvement or more reuse does not by itself justify intervention.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Connect the selected structural mechanism to an actual task, quality or product-production consequence and a cheaper alternative.
full_original.activation_guard: Refactoring, decomposition, consolidation or variability restructuring is justified by its claimed payoff.
full_original.distinctness: Service count, catalogue compliance and configuration count are distinct proxies; their common limitation does not make the mechanisms equivalent.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-025: Use a style or pattern as a conditional mechanism with an explicit problem, constraints and trade-offs; document purposeful hybrids and their interaction obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-040: Use a smell or detector output to prioritise investigation, then connect it to actual quality, invariant or change burden before prescribing repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-043: Identify the specific structural compromise, its current benefit, the future work or recurring penalty it may cause and the plausible cost of remedy; distinguish observed interest from a prediction.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-050: Select independent deployments where workload, release, failure or ownership needs warrant their distributed-system and operational costs; validate data and interaction independence.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-051: Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-058: Emergence is not a general exemption from examining architecture-relevant consequences; reason just enough, and revise as the system and knowledge change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C034: Name the recurring maintenance task and expected improvement, compare transition and opportunity costs, intervene within a justified bound and review observed task outcomes before continuing or expanding.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C035: Use metrics to identify questions and compare a declared local objective; cross-check against actual task cost and requirements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C036: Candidate treats a named pattern, tool command or catalogue count as evidence of successful improvement.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C059: Candidate forbids replacement regardless of support constraints, separability or transition evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C060: Candidate ranks maturity by platform age rather than fit, supportability and demonstrated maintenance value.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C062: Identify a concrete design/implementation condition and the future work that makes its liability actual; distinguish defects, missing features and ordinary maintenance.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C068: Candidate treats a universal index or tool-generated principal as proof of maintenance return.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C069: Reject the guarantee; require a task-specific causal account and proportionate outcome evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-015: Select among conditional code, parameters, component/plugin substitution, inheritance, aspects, feature modules and transformations according to local constraints; explicitly manage cross-mechanism interactions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-050: Reject the universal prerequisite; use the proactive, reactive, extractive or hybrid route justified by the actual starting conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-057: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-059: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.

ESA:ESA-025.bearer: Component-and-connector styles and recurring architectural solution structures.
ESA:ESA-025.authority: Designers and reviewers selecting, combining or declining architectural mechanisms. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-025.trigger: A recurring architectural problem matches the style’s assumptions closely enough to reduce design or analysis effort.

ESA:ESA-040.bearer: Potential architectural risk indicators extracted from code, graphs or review text.
ESA:ESA-040.authority: Maintainers and reviewers selecting what to investigate or repair. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-040.trigger: There are enough suspected structural problems that triage may save investigation effort.

ESA:ESA-043.bearer: Architecture-level compromises and their temporal costs.
ESA:ESA-043.authority: Maintainers and resource decision makers comparing remediation with other investments. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-043.trigger: A known architectural choice is causing or credibly expected to cause recurring change/operation burden.

ESA:ESA-050.bearer: Service decomposition and deployment topology, distinct from source-code modularity.
ESA:ESA-050.authority: Service teams and end-to-end operators/stakeholders accepting the distribution trade-off. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-050.trigger: Different parts genuinely need separate release/scaling or bounded operational control and teams can support it.

ESA:ESA-051.bearer: Logical modules within a deployment and transitions from distributed to consolidated structure.
ESA:ESA-051.authority: Application teams and operators accountable for shared deployment consequences. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-051.trigger: Shared release, scale, trust or operations make independent deployment unnecessary or harmful.

ESA:ESA-058.bearer: Architectural reasoning across time, distinct from a mandatory upfront document phase.
ESA:ESA-058.authority: Development teams and stakeholders exposed to evolving structural choices. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-058.trigger: An evolutionary or agile label is used to avoid considering a consequential interface, quality or migration decision.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C062.trigger: A structural choice plausibly increases future change cost or blocks justified evolution.

ESME:ESME-C068.bearer: Index, scoring model and future tasks. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Maintainer or sponsor relying on a cost prediction.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C069.trigger: Adjudicate when a structural metric or catalogue label is offered as sufficient benefit evidence.

ESPLE:ESPLE-057.trigger: Cloning is rejected without examining portfolio conditions or maintenance obligations.

ESPLE:ESPLE-059.trigger: Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

full_original.name: Reusable local proofs and composition premises
full_original.shared_concern: Local results transfer only through discharged semantic and realisation premises.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Check applicability, environment, interface assumptions and actual correspondence before reusing a proof or test result.
full_original.activation_guard: An acceptance argument composes local results; whole-product checks can be cheaper than reusable contracts.
full_original.distinctness: Wright connector deadlock freedom, transformation preservation, metamorphic relations and feature contracts use different semantics.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-021: Identify how entities and relations in different views correspond, then check consequential consistency and the link to implementation/configuration/operation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-022: Use a formal description when a consequential property can be expressed and analysed under a tractable model; keep the guarantee, assumptions and implementation mapping explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-068: When using the Wright/CSP formalism, establish both connector conservatism and deadlock freedom along with port/role compatibility before transferring the theorem’s deadlock-freedom result to an instantiated connector.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C030: Name the observer, relevant environment and deliberately excluded observations before claiming behaviour preservation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C031: Check the transformation’s applicability conditions and supported constructs, then validate that the implemented tool follows them.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C032: Exercise relevant tool/version transformations with targeted counterexamples, compilation, differential or other justified checks; investigate disagreements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C033: Check the actual transformed baseline using relevant semantic reasoning, tests or comparison; invalidate earlier evidence when consequential inputs change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C039: Trace acceptance expectations to independent requirements, adjudicated behaviour, domain properties or credible reference evidence; state gaps and conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C040: Choose a selection method only within its dependency/language envelope; escalate to broader execution when relevant changes fall outside it.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C044: Choose justified input/output relations, execute related cases and investigate violations while preserving the relation’s domain assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-017: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-026: Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.

ESA:ESA-068.trigger: A connector composition relies specifically on this formal deadlock-freedom guarantee.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-015: Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-030: Choose a focused prototype, simulation or analytic model for the uncertainty at hand; calibrate it where possible and distinguish omitted behaviour from demonstrated behaviour.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-031: A review can establish that a process occurred and risks were considered; it cannot by itself guarantee the real system under unexamined conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C010: Before using an evolution regularity, state its population, measure, time horizon, model and empirical exceptions; narrow or withhold the forecast when these change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C039: Trace acceptance expectations to independent requirements, adjudicated behaviour, domain properties or credible reference evidence; state gaps and conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C040: Choose a selection method only within its dependency/language envelope; escalate to broader execution when relevant changes fall outside it.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C041: Order tests by justified expected information or risk within available time, while separately deciding whether stopping early is acceptable.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C042: Use relevant mutation operators to challenge specific test weaknesses; investigate surviving mutants and equivalent or irrelevant mutants separately.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C043: Run comparable inputs against the old/new or independent implementations, locate differences and adjudicate them against intended obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C044: Choose justified input/output relations, execute related cases and investigate violations while preserving the relation’s domain assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C045: Candidate promotes test passage to complete correctness without proving coverage and oracle adequacy.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C084: Check that tests actually execute against the intended version, inputs and result criteria; challenge known failure/success controls and broken dependency assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-024: Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-025: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-026: Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-035: Reassess test-configuration validity and purpose after model change; choose repair, fresh generation or targeted new-product tests according to regression and novelty objectives.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-053: Reject the guarantee; use pairwise testing only as a bounded selection strategy within an explicit assurance argument.

full_original.shared_concern: Changes that are acceptable in isolation can alter each other's assumptions when jointly effective.

full_original.activation_guard: Independent edits, deltas, releases or runtime actions can interfere semantically.
full_original.distinctness: Textual merge, delta applicability, version skew and feature interaction are different sources of joint-state risk.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-008: Express consequential assumptions about state, control, ordering, data meaning, faults and side effects at the interface; check the assumptions actually relied on by both sides.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-009: Model or inspect the actual interaction mechanism—call, event, stream, shared store or protocol—and its control/data consequences instead of treating an arrow as self-explanatory.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-035: Allow local choices inside explicit shared contracts and escalate or negotiate only decisions that change cross-boundary consequences; preserve a way to resolve conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-047: Constrain allowed changes by the relevant system and external obligations, then assess the actual post-change state; local metric improvement is evidence for only that metric.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C022: State the consequential artefacts, consumers, dependencies and assumptions potentially affected; challenge the boundary in proportion to missed-effect consequence and reopen it when counterevidence appears.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C025: Represent the dependency types that can propagate the actual change, including build, generated, runtime, data and organisational/interface edges where consequential; distinguish observed or inferred edges from necessary ones.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C028: Check the actual merged or concurrently effective candidate against joint intent and supported effects; do not reuse isolated green results as evidence for the new combined state.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C047: Integrate at a cadence suited to actual dependencies and run evidence that can detect meaningful interaction failures; communicate failures to someone able to act.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C057: Enumerate the supported intermediate combinations and constrain activation order or feature use until each combination’s obligations hold.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C090: Use applicable static or generated-test analysis to propose potentially interfering changes, then adjudicate actual joint intent and behaviour; retain detector assumptions, false positives and missed conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C104: At the join of concurrent edits, mixed versions, data mappings and responsibility transfers, identify reachable combinations that matter to supported obligations and validate, isolate or prohibit those combinations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-016: Define applicable deltas, their dependencies or order and the validity conditions of each modification; verify the resulting product rather than assuming arbitrary edits commute.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-024: Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-032: Identify affected products and assumptions, select appropriate regression evidence and coordinate propagation, exceptions or supported parallel versions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-033: State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-044: Check the transition path, quiescence or state transfer and actual controllability; preserve safety requirements throughout the operating phase or enter a separately justified safe reconfiguration phase.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-008: Express consequential assumptions about state, control, ordering, data meaning, faults and side effects at the interface; check the assumptions actually relied on by both sides.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-046: Observe the running system, interpret observations in an architecture model, choose among allowed changes and execute them through available effectors; keep system-specific translation explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-047: Constrain allowed changes by the relevant system and external obligations, then assess the actual post-change state; local metric improvement is evidence for only that metric.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-048: An improved local objective neither authorises an architectural change nor establishes its external consequences.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-063: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-068: When using the Wright/CSP formalism, establish both connector conservatism and deadlock freedom along with port/role compatibility before transferring the theorem’s deadlock-freedom result to an instantiated connector.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C006: Authorise a bounded temporary change of objective, including disabling or degrading capability when that contains a more consequential failure; state residual obligations, accepted loss, observation and follow-up.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C049: Identify persistent and external effects, demonstrate the restoration, containment or forward-repair route actually promised, and reconsider remaining options before a transition invalidates them; obtain legitimate acceptance for residual irreversibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C055: Declare old/new data meanings, authoritative writers and reconciliation rules; check the transfer against actual data and concurrent effects instead of equating record counts or script success with preserved meaning.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C057: Enumerate the supported intermediate combinations and constrain activation order or feature use until each combination’s obligations hold.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C061: Candidate treats a code revert as proof that all deployed consequences are undone.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C094: Distinguish proposing a change, accepting its evidence and executing consequential actions; bind each to actual legitimate capability and any limited delegation. Authorisation of a goal does not automatically transfer deployment or external-state powers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C098: Revise a method, threshold or oracle only for an authorised failure/benefit hypothesis or separately authorised objective change, using evidence not constituted merely by the candidate satisfying its newly chosen rule; preserve unrelated predecessor obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C104: At the join of concurrent edits, mixed versions, data mappings and responsibility transfers, identify reachable combinations that matter to supported obligations and validate, isolate or prohibit those combinations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-013: Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-027: State the assumptions and guarantees of a feature or component and discharge compatibility and interaction obligations when composing selected parts.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-043: Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-044: Check the transition path, quiescence or state transfer and actual controllability; preserve safety requirements throughout the operating phase or enter a separately justified safe reconfiguration phase.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-045: Synthesize a supervisor for the modelled plant and requirements, then establish that observations, event controllability and actuation match the implementation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-054: Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-060: Reject self-authorising control; separately establish observation, actual actuation capability, external permission and the expected consequence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-062: Reject that stronger implication. Retain the narrower distinction that selected features are fixed after a declared binding time; analyse inputs, state, timing and environment separately.

groups.name: Shared-asset responsibility and product autonomy

full_original.name: Shared-asset responsibility and product autonomy
full_original.shared_concern: Shared decisions affect product-specific obligations without automatically creating common decision authority.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Identify affected products, responsible asset participants, practical support and a proportionate arbitration/exception path.
full_original.activation_guard: A shared asset or architecture decision crosses a product or organisational boundary.
full_original.distinctness: The same mechanism may inform several participants, but internal ownership, supplier control and autonomous product acceptance remain distinct.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-005: Make it clear who can accept a consequential trade-off, who must be consulted and who can execute it; neither identifying a concern nor holding a meeting grants permission to act.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-012: Place boundaries by considering change coupling, communication, translation and operation costs together; compare local and distributed alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-013: Identify common and varying obligations across a genuine set of related systems, then arrange abstractions and uses relations to support required variants or subsets.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-034: Identify consequential technical/work dependencies and arrange adequate communication across the people who must coordinate them; test the actual coordination problem rather than copying an organisation chart.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-035: Allow local choices inside explicit shared contracts and escalate or negotiate only decisions that change cross-boundary consequences; preserve a way to resolve conflicts.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C004: At a transfer or continuity risk, establish that an actual willing recipient has the knowledge, access, time and practical ability to perform representative supported work; use explanation, supervised work or equivalent evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C066: Identify who gains now and who must later maintain, migrate or absorb risk; involve affected decision makers to the extent needed for legitimate trade-offs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C071: Make responsibility and decision rights clear enough to resolve overlapping changes and support requests without assuming exclusive code ownership.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C072: Align promised support, intake and update obligations with available willing capacity; negotiate reduced scope, sponsorship, transfer or retirement when infeasible.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C074: Identify supported dependency versions and consequential transitive reliance; assess update, pinning, substitution or retirement against actual compatibility and support needs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C075: Identify plausible consumers through interfaces, usage, dependency data and consultation; disclose uncertainty and notify those needing action.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C076: Provide affected supported consumers with the behaviour/support change, affected versions, timing and feasible response information needed for their decision; examine whether the channel and recipient can make it operative.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-004: Maintain a functional distinction between creating family capabilities and instantiating products, with explicit exchange of requirements, constraints and feasibility evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-005: Return a product observation with its configuration, asset baseline and consequence; decide whether to repair the core, adjust a constraint, retain an exception or revise scope.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-006: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-018: Treat non-code work products as reusable assets where products actually consume them, with compatible versioning and variation information.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-019: State the architectural invariants required for reuse and the permitted substitutions; enforce or check them in the derivation path where the claim requires enforcement.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-032: Identify affected products and assumptions, select appropriate regression evidence and coordinate propagation, exceptions or supported parallel versions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-033: State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-039: Make contribution, variation and release decision rights explicit; provide a proportionate way to adjudicate competing product obligations and fund accepted shared work.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-040: Align skills, capacity, incentives and cost allocation with the intended shared-production responsibilities; scale commitments to actual capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-041: Identify who controls assets, proposals, interfaces and releases; distinguish contractual or negotiated compatibility from internal derivation authority; export bounded interfaces rather than fictitious central control.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-042: Associate externally supplied obligations with affected assets and products, then require appropriate evidence or specialist adjudication before deriving or changing those products.

ESA:ESA-005.bearer: Consequential decisions and commitments at organisational/software interfaces.
ESA:ESA-005.authority: Trade-off decision makers, implementers and affected consumers; authority is supplied by the real context, not this ledger. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-005.trigger: A change alters commitments or transfers risk/cost across roles, teams or external parties.

ESA:ESA-012.bearer: Logical, team and deployment boundary choices, which need not coincide.
ESA:ESA-012.authority: Component teams and those accountable for end-to-end delivery and operation. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-012.trigger: A boundary can reduce change propagation but creates a material coordination or runtime burden.

ESA:ESA-013.bearer: Architecture of related program families, shared assets and variation boundaries.
ESA:ESA-013.authority: Family/product architects and developers selecting valid members; economic product-line decisions remain a later interface. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-013.trigger: Multiple related products or configurations have known shared structure and deliberate variation.

ESA:ESA-034.bearer: Coupling between software/work dependencies and human communication.
ESA:ESA-034.authority: Teams and organisational decision makers able to alter coordination arrangements. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-034.trigger: Cross-team dependencies cause misunderstandings, delay or incompatible changes.

ESA:ESA-035.bearer: Architectural decision allocation across component, product and team boundaries.
ESA:ESA-035.authority: Local teams and those accountable for shared constraints; delegation is contextual rather than asserted by the method. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-035.trigger: Multiple teams need autonomy but share users, data, quality limits or release obligations.

ESME:ESME-C004.bearer: The actual recipient or continuing maintenance group and its supported work.
ESME:ESME-C004.authority: Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.
ESME:ESME-C004.trigger: Initial handover, onboarding, departure, concentration or a new support obligation threatens practical maintenance capability.

ESME:ESME-C066.bearer: Cost allocation, support promises and affected stakeholders. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C066.trigger: A local benefit shifts material work or obligations to other teams, future maintainers or external consumers.

ESME:ESME-C071.bearer: Change requests, affected components and decision responsibilities. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Contributors, maintainers and downstream users seeking a decision.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C071.trigger: Multiple contributors or support paths create ambiguity about acceptance, review or incident response.

ESME:ESME-C072.bearer: Support promises, workload, available people and tooling. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Maintainers, users relying on support and potential sponsors/successors.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C072.trigger: Demand, dependency obligations or turnover exceed sustainable support capability.

ESME:ESME-C074.bearer: Dependency manifests, resolved versions, support status and affected uses. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Upstream/downstream maintainers and operators.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C074.trigger: A dependency changes, loses support or creates a relevant defect/security obligation.

ESME:ESME-C075.bearer: Include code, API, schema, protocol, configuration, build, policy and relevant ownership/deployment state rather than a universal source-file-only graph.
ESME:ESME-C075.authority: Producers communicate change and uncertainty; independent consumers decide their own migration and acceptance.
ESME:ESME-C075.trigger: A public or shared behaviour, data format, dependency or support promise changes.

ESME:ESME-C076.bearer: Release notes, support policy, client dependencies and transition instructions. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Downstream maintainers and users able to adapt or contest the change.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESPLE:ESPLE-032.bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

ESPLE:ESPLE-033.bearer: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.

ESPLE:ESPLE-039.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.

ESPLE:ESPLE-040.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.

ESPLE:ESPLE-040.trigger: A product-line plan requires work or coordination beyond the existing organisation's supported practice.

ESPLE:ESPLE-041.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.authority: Platform maintainers and external participants negotiate evidence and compatibility; one organisation cannot unilaterally authorise changes to autonomous derivatives. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.trigger: Suppliers, open-source participants or independent platform users determine material variation.

ESPLE:ESPLE-042.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.

ESPLE:ESPLE-042.trigger: Supplier conditions, security requirements, licences, regulation or support commitments constrain valid product use.

full_original.shared_concern: The affected actor must be able to interpret and act on the relevant consequence.

ESA:ESA-005.trigger: A change alters commitments or transfers risk/cost across roles, teams or external parties.

ESA:ESA-008.bearer: Semantic contracts at component, service or connector boundaries.
ESA:ESA-008.authority: Both sides of the interface and integration reviewers; no side may silently expand the other’s obligations. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-008.trigger: Parts are composed, reused or replaced and nominal signatures do not capture their operating expectations.

ESA:ESA-034.bearer: Coupling between software/work dependencies and human communication.
ESA:ESA-034.authority: Teams and organisational decision makers able to alter coordination arrangements. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-034.trigger: Cross-team dependencies cause misunderstandings, delay or incompatible changes.

ESA:ESA-035.bearer: Architectural decision allocation across component, product and team boundaries.
ESA:ESA-035.authority: Local teams and those accountable for shared constraints; delegation is contextual rather than asserted by the method. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-035.trigger: Multiple teams need autonomy but share users, data, quality limits or release obligations.

ESA:ESA-062.bearer: Coupling between user interaction and architectural state/control mechanisms.
ESA:ESA-062.authority: Users or their representatives, interaction designers and system engineers. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-062.trigger: A user scenario cannot be met by presentation changes alone.

ESA:ESA-066.bearer: Service relationship and externally meaningful effects, not merely interface syntax.
ESA:ESA-066.authority: Providers and consumers within their real policies/contracts; each retains its actual authority boundary. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-066.trigger: A consumer relies on another participant’s capability across a service boundary.

ESME:ESME-C004.bearer: The actual recipient or continuing maintenance group and its supported work.
ESME:ESME-C004.authority: Delivering and receiving maintainers exchange knowledge; managers provide time and authority rather than infer competence from attendance.
ESME:ESME-C004.trigger: Initial handover, onboarding, departure, concentration or a new support obligation threatens practical maintenance capability.

ESME:ESME-C071.bearer: Change requests, affected components and decision responsibilities. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Contributors, maintainers and downstream users seeking a decision.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C071.trigger: Multiple contributors or support paths create ambiguity about acceptance, review or incident response.

ESME:ESME-C074.bearer: Dependency manifests, resolved versions, support status and affected uses. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Upstream/downstream maintainers and operators.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C074.trigger: A dependency changes, loses support or creates a relevant defect/security obligation.

ESME:ESME-C075.bearer: Include code, API, schema, protocol, configuration, build, policy and relevant ownership/deployment state rather than a universal source-file-only graph.
ESME:ESME-C075.authority: Producers communicate change and uncertainty; independent consumers decide their own migration and acceptance.
ESME:ESME-C075.trigger: A public or shared behaviour, data format, dependency or support promise changes.

ESME:ESME-C076.bearer: Release notes, support policy, client dependencies and transition instructions. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Downstream maintainers and users able to adapt or contest the change.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C076.trigger: A change affects consumer obligations, compatibility, support or availability.

ESME:ESME-C077.bearer: Resource, API version, support policy, deprecation date and possible sunset date. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Client developers and supported users.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C077.trigger: An interface or service is being superseded, losing guarantees or approaching shutdown.

ESME:ESME-C078.bearer: Service endpoints, users, data, credentials/access, support promises and retained records. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Remaining consumers, maintainers and authorised custodians.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C078.trigger: The software is no longer useful, supportable or justified relative to alternatives.

ESPLE:ESPLE-004.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-004.authority: Asset developers and product developers need reciprocal access to decisions; management supplies resources rather than treating a model as authority. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-004.trigger: At least one asset or production decision is intended to serve several products.

ESPLE:ESPLE-005.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-005.authority: Product engineers communicate evidence to domain maintainers; affected product owners participate when obligations change. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-005.trigger: Derivation failure, recurring local workaround, unexpected interaction or a justified new common need.

ESPLE:ESPLE-006.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-006.authority: Product and core maintainers agree who carries future changes; permission to diverge is not permission to misrepresent family assurance. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-006.trigger: A product obligation cannot be met adequately through the current shared assets without disproportionate disruption.

ESPLE:ESPLE-008.bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
ESPLE:ESPLE-008.authority: Domain experts, configurators and developers must resolve semantic disagreement; the modeller cannot decide stakeholder intent by naming a node. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-008.trigger: Features are used to negotiate products, derive artefacts or justify assurance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-011.bearer: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
ESPLE:ESPLE-011.authority: Configurators and domain experts; an explanation assists choice but must not conceal alternative repairs or silently change requirements. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-011.trigger: Configuration choices are numerous, cross-constrained or made by users without implementation expertise.

ESPLE:ESPLE-039.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-039.authority: Product and core decision-makers exchange impact and priority information; evidence of a technical opportunity is separate from authority to act. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-039.trigger: Shared changes affect products with different priorities or authorities.

ESPLE:ESPLE-041.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.authority: Platform maintainers and external participants negotiate evidence and compatibility; one organisation cannot unilaterally authorise changes to autonomous derivatives. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-041.trigger: Suppliers, open-source participants or independent platform users determine material variation.

ESPLE:ESPLE-042.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-042.authority: Product owners, relevant specialists and asset maintainers exchange obligations and impact evidence; SPLE analysis does not grant legal permission or certify security. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-042.trigger: Supplier conditions, security requirements, licences, regulation or support commitments constrain valid product use.

FULLY_ABSORBED would require actual applicable operative postcondition and qualification at the claimed layer for every positively admitted member, with adverse/research/conditional states independently retained.

full_original.name: Completion, support-aware retirement and historical retention
full_original.shared_concern: Removing new demand does not discharge older supported products, data or recovery obligations.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Check residual consumers and state obligations; retire, reclassify enduring coexistence or retain a supported historical baseline.
full_original.activation_guard: A scaffold, feature, service, record or support programme is being stopped or declared complete.
full_original.distinctness: No new products, no new changes, no running service and no retained history are four different boundaries.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-026: Compare feasible architectural options, including retaining the present design or a smaller intervention, against the same concerns and assumptions; expose excluded options.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-033: Keep a decision’s status and reopening conditions visible; distinguish superseding it from erasing the evidence that once justified it.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-044: Plan migration steps that preserve required behaviour and compatibility while old and new structures coexist; include routing/data transitions and an explicit end to temporary arrangements.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-049: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-051: Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-056: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C052: Compare feasible interventions by preserved obligations, domain recovery, data conversion, support horizon and transition cost; do not collapse all modernisation into rewriting.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C058: Keep temporary gateways and duplicate operation only while they protect a live obligation; before declaring completion or removing them, check residual consumers, data authority, supported versions and recovery needs, then close the old path or explicitly reclassify enduring coexistence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C065: Defer a structural intervention when its expected value is below its cost, while retaining a trigger to revisit if demand, risk or support changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C072: Align promised support, intake and update obligations with available willing capacity; negotiate reduced scope, sponsorship, transfer or retirement when infeasible.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C077: Declare the local meaning and support effect of deprecation, distinguishing discouraged use, changed guarantees, end of support and service termination.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C078: Identify remaining users, data, support and archival obligations; authorise termination and verify the intended services/routes actually close while agreed retained assets remain usable.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C079: Choose what must remain retrievable or executable for a declared purpose and horizon, and verify the relevant retrieval/reproduction capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C081: Choose continued unchanged operation where current obligations, support conditions and expected value do not justify intervention; keep only relevant observation triggers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C082: Use servicing-stage diagnosis to examine remaining comprehension and evolution capacity, but do not infer impossibility from the label.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C105: Evaluate the combined inquiry, validation, coordination and support arrangement against live obligations and observed outcomes; consolidate, substitute or retire controls whose consumer or protection has ended or whose cost is dominated, without silently waiving the outcome.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-006: Permit a bounded product divergence with its baseline, purpose, support responsibility and conditions for reintegration or continued separation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-031: Map old selections and product intent to a permitted new configuration, accounting for intermediate constraints, change costs and the actual resulting product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-033: State compatible baseline combinations and supported release relationships; allow coordinated or independent product schedules while making upgrade and support obligations explicit.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-054: Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-061: Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.

ESA:ESA-026.authority: Design sponsors, implementers and stakeholders accepting costs or foregone options. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-026.trigger: A consequential investment or restructuring is being justified.

ESA:ESA-033.bearer: Time-indexed architectural decisions and their dependency links.
ESA:ESA-033.authority: Maintainers and authorised decision revisers; a record itself does not grant revision authority. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-033.trigger: Architectural choices outlive their original workload, team, dependency or business assumptions.

ESA:ESA-044.bearer: Sequences and coexistence states between architectural configurations.
ESA:ESA-044.authority: Migration engineers, operators and stakeholders accepting continuity or interruption costs. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-044.trigger: A consequential replacement must proceed while service or development continues.

ESA:ESA-049.bearer: Architectural options, abstraction/variation points and temporal cost of change.

ESA:ESA-049.trigger: A proposed abstraction, extension point or distributed boundary is justified primarily by future changes.

ESA:ESA-051.bearer: Logical modules within a deployment and transitions from distributed to consolidated structure.

ESA:ESA-056.bearer: Architecture methods and governance arrangements applied to a particular system.

ESA:ESA-056.trigger: Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C079.trigger: Historical analysis, compliance, research reproduction or future revival justifies retained artefacts after active use.

ESME:ESME-C081.bearer: Current capability, support horizon and environmental assumptions. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Current users and maintainers.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C082.bearer: Remaining expertise, recoverable design knowledge and feasible change classes. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Maintainers and those choosing investment or retirement.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C105.bearer: The combined maintenance-control arrangement and its continuing consumers, protection and total burden.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESPLE:ESPLE-003.bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.

groups.name: Bounded automation versus lifecycle replacement

full_original.name: Bounded automation versus lifecycle replacement
full_original.shared_concern: Task assistance does not establish autonomous architecture, maintenance or superior product-line regeneration.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Keep suggestions as candidates; check exact outputs, intent, tool versions, authority and total work; retain unresolved broader claims.
full_original.activation_guard: Automation is proposed for a bounded task or extrapolated into a lifecycle capability.
full_original.distinctness: Architectural advice, patch repair, deterministic generation and regenerative replacement are distinct interventions with different evidence.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-054: Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-060: No general method for reliable autonomous architecting under evolving open-ended requirements is established by the examined evidence; preserve it as a research question rather than a prohibition or accepted capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C083: Treat the patch as a candidate; check intended repair, preservation, unsupported changes and uncertainty before acceptance.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C084: Check that tests actually execute against the intended version, inputs and result criteria; challenge known failure/success controls and broken dependency assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C085: Record task provenance, temporal/version scope, possible training exposure and test-oracle limits; avoid treating repeated benchmark scores as independent evidence of unseen maintenance ability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C086: Compare the stated requirement, reference change and acceptance tests; adjudicate mismatches before using them to judge another implementation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C087: Measure the end-to-end effort, latency, quality and resource costs relevant to the actual workflow against credible human/tool-assisted alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C088: Bind automation evidence to the model/tool, configuration, prompts, hardware and task envelope; recheck changed assumptions before reusing the claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C089: Choose model/quantisation settings by relevant repair quality and measured total resource constraints, not parameter count or aggregate success alone.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C094: Distinguish proposing a change, accepting its evidence and executing consequential actions; bind each to actual legitimate capability and any limited delegation. Authorisation of a goal does not automatically transfer deployment or external-state powers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C095: Investigated claim: AI assistance yields durable net improvement in maintainability after accounting for later comprehension, regressions and support.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C096: Candidate claims that successful generated patches eliminate the need to establish intent, residual evidence or accountable action.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C099: Reject the universal comparison; evaluate bounded automation by correct outcomes and complete costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C100: Withhold the general capability claim; distinguish bounded demonstrated tasks from open obligations in intent, long-term regression, review, authority and deployment.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-017: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-020: Maintain an actionable, version-related derivation procedure that tells builders which decisions, assets, tools and checks produce a supported product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-021: Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-028: Check the actual derived artefacts against the selected product obligations and operating context, reusing family evidence only where its premises apply.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-047: Treat generated changes as proposals; validate syntax, constraints, semantic intent, realisation and product obligations using appropriate independent checks before acceptance.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-048: The candidate is a replacement strategy: retain specifications and regenerate variants. Its stronger claim of superior lifecycle adequacy is not established by the inspected evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-056: Reject total automation as a universal definition; require a defined, adequate derivation method and evidence for the resulting products.

ESA:ESA-054.authority: Human or otherwise authorised reviewers who retain decision responsibility; generated text has no operative mandate. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-054.trigger: AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

ESA:ESA-060.trigger: A proposed system is expected to choose, authorise, implement and validate consequential architecture with little or no external judgement.

ESME:ESME-C100.trigger: A general unattended-maintenance claim is used to remove oversight or transfer responsibility.

ESPLE:ESPLE-017.authority: Generator maintainers and product acceptance engineers exchange failing configurations and output evidence. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-017.trigger: Product derivation relies on generation or nontrivial transformation of shared assets.

ESPLE:ESPLE-020.authority: Product builders execute the plan and return obstacles to maintainers; the plan does not itself accept a release. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-020.trigger: Products must be reproduced, handed to another team or built repeatedly from shared assets.

ESPLE:ESPLE-028.trigger: A product is delivered, deployed or materially changed.

ESPLE:ESPLE-047.authority: Modellers, maintainers and product acceptance decision-makers review the candidate; model fluency confers no mutation or release permission. ESPLE:ESPLE-048.bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-048.authority: Product and assurance owners would have to accept the replacement; the study does not authorise such adoption. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-048.trigger: Considering regeneration as a substitute for a maintained family realisation, not merely as assistance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-056.bearer: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
ESPLE:ESPLE-056.authority: Product builders and managers judge production adequacy; narrower standard or method definitions must be named rather than universalised. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-056.trigger: Automation percentage is used as the criterion for product-line existence or maturity.
