full_original.name: Learned, generated and environmental dependencies
full_original.shared_concern: Consequential behaviour can change through data, generated inputs and environment even with unchanged conventional source.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Include relevant non-code dependency and observation envelopes in impact and evidence applicability.
full_original.activation_guard: Learned components, generation or context-dependent features materially influence supported behaviour.
full_original.distinctness: A fixed feature selection does not imply fixed data or context; neither a model version nor a configuration hash alone determines behaviour.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-053: Include training/serving data, model behaviour, undeclared consumers and feedback paths in architectural reasoning; treat distribution and model changes as potential contract changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-063: Treat changes to sensors, architectural models, adaptation policies and assurance assumptions as consequential changes requiring bounded validation and continuity checks, not as automatically safe self-repair.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C003: Include build, configuration, data, documentation and other non-code objects only where a current or planned maintenance obligation depends on them.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C022: State the consequential artefacts, consumers, dependencies and assumptions potentially affected; challenge the boundary in proportion to missed-effect consequence and reopen it when counterevidence appears.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C025: Represent the dependency types that can propagate the actual change, including build, generated, runtime, data and organisational/interface edges where consequential; distinguish observed or inferred edges from necessary ones.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C091: Include data provenance, feature transformations, model versions and consequential configuration in maintenance impact and baseline reasoning.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C092: Monitor the relevant data/environment and outcome assumptions; reconsider preservation and regression evidence when those assumptions shift.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C093: Choose validation that checks the meaning and consumer of the changed artefact, including its generated or runtime effects.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C103: Track the consequential assumptions under which evidence supports a downstream claim; when an assumption changes, narrow or invalidate only dependent claims and obtain adequate replacement evidence before consequential reuse.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-013: Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-017: Validate the mapping from selections and asset versions to generated structure and behaviour, using applicable checks on transformations and produced products.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-021: Identify the configuration and the relevant asset, generator, dependency and tool versions together; distinguish requested configuration from realised product identity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-024: Identify plausible interaction mechanisms and select checks whose coverage matches their order and risk; include shared-asset and environmental interactions, not only adjacent feature-tree nodes.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-029: Include the configuration layers relevant to the claimed result and track approximation or unsupported constructs in the extraction chain.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-043: Model permitted runtime configurations, relevant context and the mapping from observations to proposed reconfiguration; connect the decision to actual actuators and feedback.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-062: Reject that stronger implication. Retain the narrower distinction that selected features are fixed after a declared binding time; analyse inputs, state, timing and environment separately.

groups.name: Resource constraints and costly flexibility

full_original.name: Resource constraints and costly flexibility
full_original.shared_concern: Assurance, variation and distribution consume resources that may outweigh the protected benefit.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Compare footprint, operation, support, evaluation and opportunity costs under explicit hard constraints.
full_original.activation_guard: The selected mechanism imposes material resource or coordination burden; unneeded machinery can be omitted.
full_original.distinctness: Energy is not lifecycle sustainability, model memory is not total repair cost, and theoretical variants are not realised value.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-012: Place boundaries by considering change coupling, communication, translation and operation costs together; compare local and distributed alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-017: Separate hard constraints from preferences, compare effects on multiple concerns and make the chosen sacrifice explicit; do not aggregate away unacceptable consequences.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-029: Establish feasible options and hard constraints first, then explore plausible costs, utilities, dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating one estimated ratio as an objective answer.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-050: Select independent deployments where workload, release, failure or ownership needs warrant their distributed-system and operational costs; validate data and interaction independence.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-051: Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-052: Model provider-managed execution and service dependencies, including data locality, lifecycle, communication, resource and failure assumptions relevant to the workload.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-055: Declare the sustainability concern and system/lifecycle boundary, then evaluate architectural alternatives against measurable impacts and competing constraints rather than assuming a fashionable deployment is greener.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-056: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C011: Use observed comprehension, review and recovery demand to constrain change intake and invest in knowledge when understanding becomes a bottleneck.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C034: Name the recurring maintenance task and expected improvement, compare transition and opportunity costs, intervene within a justified bound and review observed task outcomes before continuing or expanding.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C064: Compare intervention, validation, disruption, future support and opportunity costs under plausible scenarios; retain uncertainty and identify cost bearers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C072: Align promised support, intake and update obligations with available willing capacity; negotiate reduced scope, sponsorship, transfer or retirement when infeasible.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C087: Measure the end-to-end effort, latency, quality and resource costs relevant to the actual workflow against credible human/tool-assisted alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C089: Choose model/quantisation settings by relevant repair quality and measured total resource constraints, not parameter count or aggregate success alone.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C105: Evaluate the combined inquiry, validation, coordination and support arrangement against live obligations and observed outcomes; consolidate, substitute or retire controls whose consumer or protection has ended or whose cost is dominated, without silently waiving the outcome.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-013: Choose a binding time for each variation by weighing when information becomes available against footprint, assurance, deployment and runtime transition costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-025: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-040: Align skills, capacity, incentives and cost allocation with the intended shared-production responsibilities; scale commitments to actual capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-054: Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-059: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.

ESA:ESA-012.bearer: Logical, team and deployment boundary choices, which need not coincide.
ESA:ESA-012.authority: Component teams and those accountable for end-to-end delivery and operation. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-012.trigger: A boundary can reduce change propagation but creates a material coordination or runtime burden.

ESA:ESA-017.bearer: Multi-quality architectural alternatives and external constraints.
ESA:ESA-017.authority: Affected stakeholders and authorised trade-off decision makers. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-017.trigger: Improving one response can worsen another or transfer cost to a different stakeholder.

ESA:ESA-029.bearer: Architectural investment alternatives, costs and stakeholder preference models.
ESA:ESA-029.authority: Budget/benefit decision makers and affected stakeholders; the model advises rather than owns the decision. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-029.trigger: Several acceptable alternatives compete for constrained resources and economic consequences may change the choice.

ESA:ESA-050.bearer: Service decomposition and deployment topology, distinct from source-code modularity.
ESA:ESA-050.authority: Service teams and end-to-end operators/stakeholders accepting the distribution trade-off. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-050.trigger: Different parts genuinely need separate release/scaling or bounded operational control and teams can support it.

ESA:ESA-051.bearer: Logical modules within a deployment and transitions from distributed to consolidated structure.
ESA:ESA-051.authority: Application teams and operators accountable for shared deployment consequences. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-051.trigger: Shared release, scale, trust or operations make independent deployment unnecessary or harmful.

ESA:ESA-052.bearer: Function, platform and external-service composition in a serverless deployment.
ESA:ESA-052.authority: Application teams and provider-facing operators; provider controls constrain what the application can observe or change. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-052.trigger: A design delegates execution/resource management to a serverless platform.

ESA:ESA-055.bearer: Architectural choices affecting operational and lifecycle resource consequences.
ESA:ESA-055.authority: Stakeholders setting impact priorities and engineers able to measure and alter relevant mechanisms. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-055.trigger: Energy, emissions, resource use or longer-term maintainability are material stakeholder concerns.

ESA:ESA-056.bearer: Architecture methods and governance arrangements applied to a particular system.
ESA:ESA-056.authority: Those using and funding architectural work, with affected stakeholders participating in trade-offs. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-056.trigger: Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C064.trigger: Competing repairs, features, structural improvements or retirement choices draw on limited resources.

ESME:ESME-C072.bearer: Support promises, workload, available people and tooling. People, ownership, documentation, dependency graphs, support policies, releases and archives all matter.

authority.actors: Maintainers, users relying on support and potential sponsors/successors.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C072.trigger: Demand, dependency obligations or turnover exceed sustainable support capability.

ESME:ESME-C087.bearer: Human tasks, model calls, review effort, compute and accepted outcomes. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.

authority.actors: Maintainers and sponsors bearing both visible and shifted costs.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C087.trigger: Automation adoption is justified as saving maintenance effort or increasing useful output.

ESME:ESME-C089.bearer: Model, quantisation, hardware, repair instances and resource measurements. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.

authority.actors: Maintainer/operator constrained by compute and accepted repair quality.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C089.trigger: Resource-limited repair automation makes memory, energy or time consequential.

ESME:ESME-C105.bearer: The combined maintenance-control arrangement and its continuing consumers, protection and total burden.

authority.actors: Maintainers and affected stakeholders deciding acceptable evidence and coordination.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C105.trigger: Several controls interact, compete for finite maintenance capacity or persist after their original obligations change.

ESPLE:ESPLE-003.bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
ESPLE:ESPLE-003.authority: Product sponsors and shared-asset maintainers negotiate the scope; this criterion does not require a new board for each feature. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-003.trigger: A request to broaden the set of products or selectable behaviours.

ESPLE:ESPLE-013.bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
ESPLE:ESPLE-013.authority: Product architects, build/deployment engineers and operators where relevant; runtime rebinding needs actual operational permission. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-013.trigger: A variation point is introduced or its resolution time changes.

ESPLE:ESPLE-025.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.authority: Test planners and assurance consumers choose the coverage trade-off; a sampler cannot declare all unsampled products correct. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.trigger: Full enumeration is infeasible and a bounded sample can provide useful assurance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-036.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.authority: Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.trigger: An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

ESPLE:ESPLE-040.bearer: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE:ESPLE-040.authority: Engineering managers, product teams and sponsors negotiate resourcing; training completion alone does not establish operational capability. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-040.trigger: A product-line plan requires work or coordination beyond the existing organisation's supported practice.

ESPLE:ESPLE-054.bearer: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
ESPLE:ESPLE-054.authority: Architects and operators assess the actual need for late choice; flexibility is not an end in itself. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-054.trigger: A compile/deployment-time choice is moved later without a concrete operational need.

ESPLE:ESPLE-059.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.authority: Portfolio and assurance planners interpret the count; a metric collector cannot infer market value from arithmetic. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.trigger: Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-006: Candidate shorthand groups salient decisions, but without a scope or consequence test it does not determine what architectural work should occur.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-025: Use a style or pattern as a conditional mechanism with an explicit problem, constraints and trade-offs; document purposeful hybrids and their interaction obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-036: No deterministic rule mapping an organisation chart to software architecture is admitted; communication and technical structures influence each other under contingent conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-057: The useful warning is retained through separate REST constraints (ESA-065) and service interaction/effect contracts (ESA-066), whose assumptions and consumers differ.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-058: Emergence is not a general exemption from examining architecture-relevant consequences; reason just enough, and revise as the system and knowledge change.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-059: Conformance of an architecture description is not admitted as a certificate that the actual architecture satisfies stakeholder concerns.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C002: Use purpose labels alongside observable activity and artefact scope, permitting multiple purposes; include additive and emergency distinctions when using the 2022 terminology.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C007: Candidate proposes requiring every maintenance activity to fit exactly one of four boxes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C009: Candidate treats chronological age or lack of feature growth as sufficient grounds for intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C012: Candidate fixes staffing, effort or delivery-rate predictions as invariant across organisations and tool/environment changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C018: Distinguish analysis that changes a representation or understanding from an intervention that alters the subject system; describe the actual abstraction level and effects.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C036: Candidate treats a named pattern, tool command or catalogue count as evidence of successful improvement.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-026: Compare feasible architectural options, including retaining the present design or a smaller intervention, against the same concerns and assumptions; expose excluded options.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-049: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-056: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C008: Observe changes in use, expectations and constraints; decide whether adaptation, servicing, unchanged operation or retirement best preserves justified usefulness.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C009: Candidate treats chronological age or lack of feature growth as sufficient grounds for intervention.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C050: Choose a small repair when it satisfies the obligation at lower expected total cost and risk than structural transformation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C051: Assess obligations, supportability and change cost directly; treat age as a possible clue, not proof that replacement is needed.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C052: Compare feasible interventions by preserved obligations, domain recovery, data conversion, support horizon and transition cost; do not collapse all modernisation into rewriting.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C059: Candidate forbids replacement regardless of support constraints, separability or transition evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C060: Candidate ranks maturity by platform age rather than fit, supportability and demonstrated maintenance value.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C065: Defer a structural intervention when its expected value is below its cost, while retaining a trigger to revisit if demand, risk or support changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C078: Identify remaining users, data, support and archival obligations; authorise termination and verify the intended services/routes actually close while agreed retained assets remain usable.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C081: Choose continued unchanged operation where current obligations, support conditions and expected value do not justify intervention; keep only relevant observation triggers.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-050: Reject the universal prerequisite; use the proactive, reactive, extractive or hybrid route justified by the actual starting conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-054: Reject a universal ranking and select binding time by the timing of needed knowledge and the costs of retained flexibility.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-057: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-061: Distinguish admission to new products from continued support of existing ones; retire or bind variability when its consumer disappears, preserving required historical baselines and migration paths.

differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C029: Identify supported releases/configurations and the obligations shared or different across them; select evidence by actual support promises and interaction risk.

differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C097: Candidate elevates all observed legacy behaviour to a perpetual requirement.

full_original.name: Causal liabilities and prospective payoff
full_original.shared_concern: A predicted future burden needs a specific change/use scenario and an affected cost bearer.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Retain an actionable liability and compare repay/defer/retire branches; observe actual task consequences.
full_original.activation_guard: Debt or shared-asset investment is proposed as the reason to restructure.
full_original.distinctness: Architectural debt, maintenance debt and variation synchronisation cost can overlap without being independent monetary quantities.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-027: Walk representative modifications through an architecture, identify affected elements and interacting scenarios, and compare the resulting burdens across alternatives.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-029: Establish feasible options and hard constraints first, then explore plausible costs, utilities, dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating one estimated ratio as an objective answer.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-043: Identify the specific structural compromise, its current benefit, the future work or recurring penalty it may cause and the plausible cost of remedy; distinguish observed interest from a prediction.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-049: Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C034: Name the recurring maintenance task and expected improvement, compare transition and opportunity costs, intervene within a justified bound and review observed task outcomes before continuing or expanding.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C035: Use metrics to identify questions and compare a declared local objective; cross-check against actual task cost and requirements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C062: Identify a concrete design/implementation condition and the future work that makes its liability actual; distinguish defects, missing features and ordinary maintenance.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C063: Record only enough evidence about an important liability, affected work, uncertainty and intended decision for the people prioritising it.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C064: Compare intervention, validation, disruption, future support and opportunity costs under plausible scenarios; retain uncertainty and identify cost bearers.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C065: Defer a structural intervention when its expected value is below its cost, while retaining a trigger to revisit if demand, risk or support changes.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C066: Identify who gains now and who must later maintain, migrate or absorb risk; involve affected decision makers to the extent needed for legitimate trade-offs.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C067: Candidate requires all debt items to be eliminated irrespective of future use, opportunity cost or retirement.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C068: Candidate treats a universal index or tool-generated principal as proof of maintenance return.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C069: Reject the guarantee; require a task-specific causal account and proportionate outcome evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-003: Admit a new variation only with a product or credible future need, an implementation boundary, an assurance consequence and an identified support cost.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-007: Choose anticipatory domain investment, incremental extension or recovery from existing variants according to uncertainty, existing assets and available migration capacity.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-038: Reassess future costs and obligations at material changes; narrow, split, retire or continue the family based on prospective adequacy, preserving outstanding support.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-057: Reject universal inadmissibility; compare cloning's immediate adequacy and future synchronisation costs with the actual product-line alternative.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-059: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.

ESA:ESA-027.bearer: Architecture under prospective functional or quality-related modifications.
ESA:ESA-027.authority: Evaluators and maintainers choosing a design or restructuring. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-027.trigger: Modifiability or the consequences of planned change are material and can be expressed as concrete scenarios.

ESA:ESA-029.bearer: Architectural investment alternatives, costs and stakeholder preference models.
ESA:ESA-029.authority: Budget/benefit decision makers and affected stakeholders; the model advises rather than owns the decision. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-029.trigger: Several acceptable alternatives compete for constrained resources and economic consequences may change the choice.

ESA:ESA-043.bearer: Architecture-level compromises and their temporal costs.
ESA:ESA-043.authority: Maintainers and resource decision makers comparing remediation with other investments. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-043.trigger: A known architectural choice is causing or credibly expected to cause recurring change/operation burden.

ESA:ESA-049.bearer: Architectural options, abstraction/variation points and temporal cost of change.
ESA:ESA-049.authority: Designers and investment decision makers accepting current complexity for future capability. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-049.trigger: A proposed abstraction, extension point or distributed boundary is justified primarily by future changes.

ESME:ESME-C034.bearer: Structure, expected change scenarios and intervention effort. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.actors: Future maintainers and those bearing current conversion cost.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C034.trigger: Repeated or credible upcoming work is materially hindered by the current structure and a feasible change may improve it.

ESME:ESME-C035.bearer: Metric definition, affected structure and real maintenance tasks. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.actors: Maintainer or planner interpreting the signal.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C035.trigger: A metric might reveal a bottleneck not already understood.

ESME:ESME-C062.bearer: Debt condition, cause, affected future change and support horizon. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Future maintainers and value/cost decision makers.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C062.trigger: A structural choice plausibly increases future change cost or blocks justified evolution.

ESME:ESME-C063.bearer: Debt item, supporting observations, cost estimates and decision history. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Maintainer, budget holder and affected downstream cost bearer.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C063.trigger: A significant liability risks being forgotten, misunderstood or shifted across teams.

ESME:ESME-C064.bearer: Maintenance options, benefits, cost horizon and uncertainty. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Stakeholders allocating effort and those who bear downstream costs.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C064.trigger: Competing repairs, features, structural improvements or retirement choices draw on limited resources.

ESME:ESME-C065.bearer: Deferred liability, prospective demand and revisit condition. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Those bearing future effort and present opportunity cost.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C065.trigger: Future change demand is uncertain, interest is small, or the system may retire before repayment benefits arise.

ESME:ESME-C066.bearer: Cost allocation, support promises and affected stakeholders. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Present and future maintainers, sponsors and downstream users.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C066.trigger: A local benefit shifts material work or obligations to other teams, future maintainers or external consumers.

ESME:ESME-C067.bearer: Debt inventory and maintenance budget. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Those needing useful current and future software.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C067.trigger: A programme treats the debt count as a target to drive to zero.

ESME:ESME-C068.bearer: Index, scoring model and future tasks. A debt item links a concrete design/implementation condition to affected future work and its economic context.

authority.actors: Maintainer or sponsor relying on a cost prediction.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C068.trigger: A decision claims certain savings from score improvement without task evidence.

ESME:ESME-C069.bearer: Bind before/after source, language/tool version, configuration and persistent representations to the actual applied transformation.
ESME:ESME-C069.authority: Metric producers do not determine product value; affected maintainers and users supply task evidence.
ESME:ESME-C069.trigger: Adjudicate when a structural metric or catalogue label is offered as sufficient benefit evidence.

ESPLE:ESPLE-003.bearer: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
ESPLE:ESPLE-003.authority: Product sponsors and shared-asset maintainers negotiate the scope; this criterion does not require a new board for each feature. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-003.trigger: A request to broaden the set of products or selectable behaviours.

ESPLE:ESPLE-007.bearer: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE:ESPLE-007.authority: Portfolio sponsors and engineering leads select a transition strategy; a tool supplier's capability does not determine organisational readiness. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-007.trigger: Starting a product line or changing how an existing portfolio is produced.

ESPLE:ESPLE-036.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.authority: Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.trigger: An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

ESPLE:ESPLE-038.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-038.authority: Portfolio sponsors with product and asset maintainers decide future investment; sunk costs explain history but cannot by themselves justify continuation. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-038.trigger: Demand changes, reuse disappoints, coordination dominates or the product portfolio contracts.

ESPLE:ESPLE-057.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-057.authority: Product and portfolio owners choose a strategy; no favourable case study establishes a universal winner. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-057.trigger: Cloning is rejected without examining portfolio conditions or maintenance obligations.

ESPLE:ESPLE-059.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.authority: Portfolio and assurance planners interpret the count; a metric collector cannot infer market value from arithmetic. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.trigger: Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

groups.name: Proportionate knowledge and control forms

full_original.name: Proportionate knowledge and control forms
full_original.shared_concern: Required distinctions and protected outcomes, not document/tool/meeting counts, determine adequate form.
full_original.shared_mechanism: Choose the smallest coherent view, explanation, review or analysis; retain escalation on consequential uncertainty.
full_original.activation_guard: A proposed form costs more than needed or a cheaper form might omit a consequential distinction.
full_original.distinctness: A local walkthrough, slice, variability model and joint control arrangement are distinct forms and may legitimately be absent.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-020: Select viewpoints by the concerns and decisions they enable, then create only the views needed to communicate or analyse those concerns.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-021: Identify how entities and relations in different views correspond, then check consequential consistency and the link to implementation/configuration/operation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-023: Completing a prescribed view set regardless of its consumers is ceremony, not a generally useful mechanism.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-024: Combine appropriate static, configuration, dynamic and human evidence to reconstruct only the architectural facts needed; label extraction scope, ambiguity and unobserved behaviour.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-037: Document quantity alone is not retained as a proxy for architectural knowledge, correctness or maintenance value.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-056: Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C013: Establish enough understanding to discriminate the pending change decision; expand inquiry when observed contradictions or impact escape invalidate that boundary.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C014: Use a declared slicing criterion and static dependence model to find potentially relevant statements, with explicit language, alias and environment assumptions.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C015: Trace a relevant execution and its data/control effects to answer a bounded question, retaining the input, environment and observation criterion.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C017: Produce or refresh a description only when a maintainer or downstream consumer needs it, and check it against the current subject.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C019: Candidate blocks every local change until the entire system and all tacit intent are recovered.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C021: Choose static, dynamic, historical and human views for the question; reconcile consequential disagreement instead of treating agreement or diagram completeness as proof.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C101: Strip the mandatory ritual while preserving appropriate authorisation, consultation and evidence; use a fuller forum only when conflicts or obligations require it.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C105: Evaluate the combined inquiry, validation, coordination and support arrangement against live obligations and observed outcomes; consolidate, substitute or retire controls whose consumer or protection has ended or whose cost is dominated, without silently waiving the outcome.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-011: Relate a conflict or forced choice to the smallest useful set of decisions and constraints; permit human correction and show relevant provenance.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-012: Use the least expressive representation that preserves required distinctions; verify translations and tool support for the actual language level.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-014: Preserve the feature-to-artefact relations needed for derivation, change impact and diagnosis, including build selection, generator input and shared implementation.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-018: Treat non-code work products as reusable assets where products actually consume them, with compatible versioning and variation information.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-026: Preserve variation symbolically or structurally during analysis so common computations are reused, while retaining conditions under which each result applies.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-037: Compare SPLE with clone-and-own, selective component reuse, a modular single product or independent development under the same quality and support obligations.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-051: Reject artefact sufficiency; require meaningful features, usable constraints, a relation to realisation and an actual configuration or change consumer.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-056: Reject total automation as a universal definition; require a defined, adequate derivation method and evidence for the resulting products.

ESA:ESA-020.bearer: Architecture descriptions and viewpoint conventions at concern-specific abstraction levels.
ESA:ESA-020.authority: Description authors and the actual stakeholders or analysts using each view. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-020.trigger: One representation obscures materially different structural, runtime, deployment or development questions.

ESA:ESA-021.bearer: Cross-view and description–implementation relations, not visual layout similarity.
ESA:ESA-021.authority: Design, deployment, development and evaluation participants relying on combined descriptions. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-021.trigger: A decision combines claims from several views or uses a model as evidence about implementation.

ESA:ESA-023.bearer: An unconditional documentation ritual rather than a system property.
ESA:ESA-023.authority: Documentation consumers and reviewers, not a template’s nominal owner. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-023.trigger: A review treats the existence of all five views as evidence of architectural adequacy.

ESA:ESA-024.bearer: Inferred architectural structures and behaviours from realised artefacts.
ESA:ESA-024.authority: Maintainers, migration designers and reviewers who need specific missing knowledge. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-024.trigger: Reliable architectural knowledge is missing or an existing description is suspect.

ESA:ESA-037.bearer: Documentation volume as a candidate architectural quality indicator.
ESA:ESA-037.authority: Document authors, maintainers and the users of their explanations. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-037.trigger: Page counts, completed templates or a large repository of records are used as assurance.

ESA:ESA-056.bearer: Architecture methods and governance arrangements applied to a particular system.
ESA:ESA-056.authority: Those using and funding architectural work, with affected stakeholders participating in trade-offs. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-056.trigger: Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

ESME:ESME-C013.bearer: The affected feature and evidence needed for the current decision. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: Maintainer and reviewer who must act, with domain experts where intent is lost.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C013.trigger: A maintainer cannot explain the relevant effect or uncertainty of a proposed intervention.

ESME:ESME-C014.bearer: Program statements, variable criterion and control/data dependencies. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: The observation specified by the slicing criterion, not every external effect.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C014.trigger: A consequential comprehension or impact question benefits from model-based relevance beyond a single observed run.

ESME:ESME-C015.bearer: Trace, instrumentation, inputs and runtime configuration. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: The observed run and selected values/events.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C015.trigger: Observed behaviour or a concrete failure requires an execution-specific explanation.

ESME:ESME-C017.bearer: Documentation and its source artefact/version. Relevant source, executable traces, build descriptions, documents and human knowledge form different evidence views.

authority.actors: The intended reader performing a named maintenance or operational task.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-015: Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-018: Validate important predictions against observations whose workload, faults, configuration and measurement boundary are representative of the decision; distinguish the measurement from the whole quality claim.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-028: Bring business/mission drivers, architecture and quality scenarios into a structured review to identify assumptions, risks, sensitivity points and trade-offs that need a decision.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-029: Establish feasible options and hard constraints first, then explore plausible costs, utilities, dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating one estimated ratio as an objective answer.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-031: A review can establish that a process occurred and risks were considered; it cannot by itself guarantee the real system under unexamined conditions.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-054: Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-060: No general method for reliable autonomous architecting under evolving open-ended requirements is established by the examined evidence; preserve it as a research question rather than a prohibition or accepted capability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C010: Before using an evolution regularity, state its population, measure, time horizon, model and empirical exceptions; narrow or withhold the forecast when these change.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C023: Use co-change suggestions to direct inspection; verify semantic or organisational relevance before adding an obligation.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C024: Candidate automatically edits every co-changed entity or treats absent co-change as proof of independence.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C035: Use metrics to identify questions and compare a declared local objective; cross-check against actual task cost and requirements.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C045: Candidate promotes test passage to complete correctness without proving coverage and oracle adequacy.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C073: Use the estimate to ask who can actually support critical work; verify with maintainers rather than treating a computed number as a failure probability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C080: Candidate assumes a widely used package cannot lose maintainers or support.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C085: Record task provenance, temporal/version scope, possible training exposure and test-oracle limits; avoid treating repeated benchmark scores as independent evidence of unseen maintenance ability.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C095: Investigated claim: AI assistance yields durable net improvement in maintainability after accounting for later comprehension, regressions and support.
differing_mechanisms.ESME:ESME-C100: Withhold the general capability claim; distinguish bounded demonstrated tasks from open obligations in intent, long-term regression, review, authority and deployment.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-023: State each assurance claim's object, quantified configurations, inputs, environment and baseline; identify the realisation obligations needed to carry it to a product.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-025: Sample valid configurations using a declared objective and budget, include critical known combinations, and report residual higher-order or environmental coverage limits.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-036: Compare lifecycle costs and required outcomes over an explicit horizon; vary demand, reuse rate and maintenance assumptions rather than rely on a universal break-even count.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-048: The candidate is a replacement strategy: retain specifications and regenerate variants. Its stronger claim of superior lifecycle adequacy is not established by the inspected evidence.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-049: No general mechanism supports the universal threshold. Replace the claim with a horizon-specific comparison of investment, derivation, coordination and support costs.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-053: Reject the guarantee; use pairwise testing only as a bounded selection strategy within an explicit assurance argument.
differing_mechanisms.ESPLE:ESPLE-059: Use counts to estimate analysis, support or selection complexity; assess value through useful products and avoided costs rather than raw combinatorics.

ESA:ESA-015.bearer: Scenario population, sampling and prioritisation at evaluation scope.
ESA:ESA-015.authority: Evaluators and affected participants, including dissenting or absent-user representatives where warranted. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-015.trigger: An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

ESA:ESA-018.bearer: Empirical evidence about realised architectural behaviour, not just models.
ESA:ESA-018.authority: Testers, operators and decision makers relying on measured outcomes. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-018.trigger: A prototype, benchmark, trace or field observation is being used to accept an architecture.

ESA:ESA-028.bearer: Multi-quality evaluation of an architectural candidate.
ESA:ESA-028.authority: Stakeholders, evaluation facilitators and people authorised to accept or mitigate the identified risks. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-028.trigger: Several consequential qualities interact and missing assumptions justify a facilitated multi-stakeholder review.

ESA:ESA-029.bearer: Architectural investment alternatives, costs and stakeholder preference models.
ESA:ESA-029.authority: Budget/benefit decision makers and affected stakeholders; the model advises rather than owns the decision. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-029.trigger: Several acceptable alternatives compete for constrained resources and economic consequences may change the choice.

ESA:ESA-031.bearer: Inference from evaluation process completion to realised performance or correctness.
ESA:ESA-031.authority: People accepting a design or relying on its review status. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-031.trigger: An approval, risk list or completed workshop is used as conclusive evidence that the system will meet its qualities.

ESA:ESA-054.bearer: AI-produced architectural representations, options, risk analyses and boundary proposals.
ESA:ESA-054.authority: Human or otherwise authorised reviewers who retain decision responsibility; generated text has no operative mandate. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-054.trigger: AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

ESA:ESA-060.bearer: Autonomous architecture decision and change process under open-ended requirements.
ESA:ESA-060.authority: Researchers and anyone proposing delegated architectural authority; the evidence does not supply that delegation. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.
ESA:ESA-060.trigger: A proposed system is expected to choose, authorise, implement and validate consequential architecture with little or no external judgement.

authority.actors: Maintainer deciding what to inspect, not automatically what to edit.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C035.bearer: Metric definition, affected structure and real maintenance tasks. Use exact pre/post code, language/tool versions and relevant runtime, persistence and external-interface context.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

authority.actors: Researchers and maintainers deciding transfer from benchmark to practice.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C095.bearer: Accepted generated changes, later maintenance tasks, regressions and total lifecycle costs. Identify issue text, reference patch, model/tool version, prompt, dataset, harness, repository state and non-code dependencies.

authority.actors: Future maintainers and sponsors, not only benchmark operators.
authority.boundary: Understanding or recommending a change does not itself authorise altering another actor’s obligations. Use actual agreed decision rights and capability; no new role or veto is created by this record.

ESME:ESME-C095.trigger: A decision generalises short-run scores or time savings to multi-release lifecycle benefit.

ESME:ESME-C100.bearer: Identify repository/task baseline, tool/model version, prompts/configuration relevant to evaluation, tests and data/model/policy artefacts. Record benchmark version and excluded cases.
ESME:ESME-C100.authority: Tool evaluators establish evidence; service/repository owners decide permissible delegation; the claimed capability does not create authority.
ESME:ESME-C100.trigger: A general unattended-maintenance claim is used to remove oversight or transfer responsibility.

ESPLE:ESPLE-023.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-023.authority: Assurance reviewers and release decision-makers consume bounded claims; analysts do not acquire release authority by producing evidence. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-023.trigger: A model, test, proof or analysis result is used to justify a product or family decision.

ESPLE:ESPLE-025.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.authority: Test planners and assurance consumers choose the coverage trade-off; a sampler cannot declare all unsampled products correct. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-025.trigger: Full enumeration is infeasible and a bounded sample can provide useful assurance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-036.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.authority: Portfolio sponsors and engineering managers review estimates with those bearing the costs; an economic model is not a realised-return measurement. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-036.trigger: An investment or continuation decision depends on product-line benefits.

ESPLE:ESPLE-048.bearer: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-048.authority: Product and assurance owners would have to accept the replacement; the study does not authorise such adoption. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-048.trigger: Considering regeneration as a substitute for a maintained family realisation, not merely as assistance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-049.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-049.authority: Investment decision-makers should demand a local comparison, not treat a published example as a rule. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-049.trigger: A proposed adoption is justified by reaching a supposedly universal number of products.

ESPLE:ESPLE-053.bearer: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE:ESPLE-053.authority: Test and acceptance decision-makers distinguish coverage from correctness; the sampling tool cannot make that stronger claim. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-053.trigger: A pairwise coverage percentage is presented as complete family assurance.

ESPLE:ESPLE-059.bearer: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.authority: Portfolio and assurance planners interpret the count; a metric collector cannot infer market value from arithmetic. A diagnosis, model result or recommendation is not by itself authorisation, capacity to execute, or evidence that the consequence occurred.
ESPLE:ESPLE-059.trigger: Configuration-space size is used in an investment or maturity claim.

full_original.shared_concern: Consequential requirements must remain connected to the responsibilities and derivation choices that realise them.

differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-002: Connect each material concern to an architectural question, a scenario or constraint and the decision that consumes it; expose conflicts and missing participation.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-014: Express a quality concern through stimulus, source, environment, affected artefact, response and response measure, tailoring detail to the decision being made.
differing_mechanisms.ESA:ESA-017: Separate hard constraints from preferences, compare effects on multiple concerns and make the chosen sacrifice explicit; do not aggregate away unacceptable consequences.

group_discriminators.current_group_discriminator: Acceptance must retain scenario/workload/configuration population and hard quality trade-offs, including excluded or harmed classes.
A cold successor must recover rationale, uncertainty and reopening condition from accessible content; a hash or recovered graph alone is insufficient.
The smallest coherent knowledge/control form must preserve decision-bearing content while permitting omission of unneeded artifacts.
A model/solver or generated-artifact pass must not become acceptance of the actual product without correspondence and use evidence.
Selected tests/configurations must preserve oracle validity and exclusions; pairwise coverage or prioritisation cannot imply exhaustive correctness.
A claim must retain its own population, access limits, horizon and dependence cluster; multiple lineage reports do not create independent evidence.
An accepted assignment must correspond to available capability and support, without deriving team topology from conceptual integrity.
Evidence, role names and tools must not supply another actor's decision right, permission or practical ability to act.
Observed old behaviour and stable names must be distinguished from surviving commitments and an authorised intended difference.
An authorised revision may change architecture or commonality while preserving actual surviving promises and support.
Recovery must observe the required function/state/authority after real actuation; valid static configurations do not establish transition safety.
A structural intervention must change the protected task or quality outcome beyond service count, catalogue compliance or variant-count proxies.
No-change, local work, traceable cloning, non-family production or justified replacement must remain feasible outcomes under actual obligations.
A dependency that changes the decision must retain its type and uncertainty; co-change or a source graph cannot create a hard scheduling edge.
A migration must provide a permissible continuation for actual state, version/configuration and irreversible history, not merely copy state or validate v2.
The decision must retain no-change/replace/retire alternatives, cost bearers and unknown horizon instead of treating prior investment as a veto.
Debt or synchronisation cost requires an actionable liability, comparator and future task consequence; imperfection and duplicated cost categories are insufficient.
Bounded AI proposals require exact-output validation while unresolved autonomous architecting/maintenance/regeneration claims remain research questions.
A shared variation boundary must earn its future support burden under plausible extensions; code resemblance cannot establish that case.
Stopping new admissions or closing a release must not erase older consumers, pending work, retained history or the actionable SSS frontier.
Flexibility/energy/resource choices must retain complete operating/support costs and hard constraints; raw configuration count is not value.
Translation must preserve the consumer-relevant semantics and explicit loss boundaries; equivalent names/configuration sets cannot imply historical or behavioural equivalence.
Fixed feature selection and code hashes must not hide changed data/model/generator/environment semantics.
